Retrieved 2014-11-15 In the wake of Pamela Hayden's retirement in November 2024, it was confirmed that her characters, including Milhouse, would be recast in the future.{{cite news|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/tv/tv-news/the-simpsons-milhouse-voice-actor-pamela-hayden-retiring-1236067689/|title='The Simpsons' Voice Actor Pamela Hayden Retiring After 35 Years|first=Rick|last=Porter|work=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|date=November 20, 2024|accessdate=November 20, 2024}} Following Hayden's appearance in ''The Simpsons'' [[Disney+]] special "[[O C'mon All Ye Faithful]]", ''Simpsons'' creator Matt Groening and writer [[Carolyn Omine]] revealed to ''Comic Book.com'' that Hayden would make a few more performances than initially announced.{{cite news|url=https://comicbook.com/anime/news/the-simpsons-christmas-disney-plus-pamela-hayden/|title=The Simpsons' Disney+ Christmas Special Brings Back Retired Star (& They Aren't Done Yet)|first=Nick|last=Valdez|publisher=Comic Book.com|date=December 17, 2024|accessdate=December 17, 2024}} As of the end of season 36, Milhouse is now voiced by singer and actor Kelly Macleod. == Profile == Milhouse is of Italian, Greek, Danish and Dutch descent, based on comments and characters introduced throughout the series. He shares the same physical features as both his parents, and his father's primary personality features (which include disappointment, insecurity, and generally depressed demeanor). Milhouse is constantly bullied by [[Nelson Muntz]], [[List of recurring The Simpsons characters#Jimbo Jones|Jimbo Jones]], [[List of recurring The Simpsons characters#Dolph Starbeam|Dolph Starbeam]], and [[List of recurring The Simpsons characters#Kearney Zzyzwicz|Kearney Zzyzwicz]], to the point that when Bart questions Milhouse by saying: "Milhouse! I thought you had a three o'clock [[wedgie]] with Nelson" in the episode "[[Little Orphan Millie]]"; Milhouse simply responds: "I had to reschedule". [[Lisa Simpson| Lisa]] has also described Milhouse as "the class [[nerd]]'. The schoolyard bullies often victimize the socially and physically awkward Milhouse, who wears thick eyeglasses, without which he cannot see. Milhouse and family are among the few Springfield residents with visible eyebrows, which are rather thick. Although not disliked and having a moderate number of friends among other kids from school aside from Bart himself, Milhouse has made a career of getting victimized, although his overall true antagonists are the schoolyard bullies of [[Springfield (The Simpsons)#Springfield Elementary School|Springfield Elementary School]] (Nelson, Jimbo, Dolph, and Kearney). In "[[Sideshow Bob Roberts]]", Jimbo, Dolph, and Kearney wrapped Milhouse in [[bumper sticker]]s and placed him in a [[shopping cart]]. After Jimbo claimed that "the [[mummy]]'s ready for his mystical journey!", the bullies pushed the cart with Milhouse down a very steep hill. He is harmed frequently, and on some occasions is injured by dangerous hazards, e.g., being run over by a train, falling down a waterfall, receiving electrical shocks, having his head polished to bone, and having his teeth knocked out by a hockey puck. As a lead character he always survives and recovers, often with no further mention of any injuries. He frequently visited a female psychiatrist until even she could not deal with his constant calling and blocked his number. On one occasion, Bart got Milhouse placed on the [[FBI Ten Most Wanted Fugitives|FBI's Most Wanted List]] even though they are friends, and tried to lure Milhouse into a cactus. Milhouse is not always subservient to Bart; in "[[Bart Sells His Soul]]", Milhouse toyed with Bart's anxiety after Bart sold his soul for $5, and Milhouse demanded $50 to return it. On another occasion, Bart introduced Milhouse to his girlfriend and had to explain why he and Milhouse are friends, but could not come up with a good answer and admitted it was due to geographical convenience. Bart did admit in "[[Little Orphan Millie]]" that he loves Milhouse.Bart: ''"Oh, I love him so much!"'' Homer also sometimes makes fun of Milhouse (once referring to Milhouse in the boy's presence as "that little wiener"). In "[[Burns, Baby Burns]]", Larry, [[Mr. Burns]]' son, brings Homer to eat at his house. Mr. Burns was angry and he asks Homer if his son "brings home nitwits and make you talk to them", to which Homer answers "Oh, all the time! Have you ever heard of this kid Milhouse? He's a little wiener who...", before being interrupted by Burns. In an attempt to purposefully enrage his father, Bart once stated that he felt "a little attracted to Milhouse", sending Homer into a rage. Bart and Milhouse appear to be the same height, but in the episode "[[Radioactive Man (The Simpsons episode)|Radioactive Man]]", it is revealed that Milhouse is at least {{convert|1|in|abbr=on}} taller than Bart. Milhouse is frequently the butt of a variety of jokes, such as being beaten up by Nelson for delivering a love note from Lisa (which Nelson thought was from Milhouse himself), having the door slammed in his face while playing [[pin the tail on the donkey]], having his possible budding homosexuality given away by his school counselor to Homer and Marge by accidentally picking up the wrong folder while discussing Bart, making him a wanted fugitive (see above), and inadvertently inheriting Bart's dismal permanent record at school through a side deal arranged between Bart, Edna Krabappel and [[Principal Skinner]], which will disqualify Milhouse from "all but the hottest and noisiest jobs". He is fluent in [[Italian language|Italian]] ("[[The Last of the Red Hat Mamas]]") due to visiting his maternal grandmother in [[Tuscany]] for two weeks every year. She hates the English language and would beat him whenever he spoke English, so he was forced to learn Italian. He began bed-wetting from this experience. He helps Lisa learn Italian, but there is no reference to his Italian background or language skills in any other episode. Milhouse's personality drastically changes when speaking Italian, becoming a suave, confident ladies' man popular with Springfield's [[Italian Americans|Italian community]] in the episode. It is later revealed that both Milhouse's middle name and his maternal family name are "[[Mussolini family|Mussolini]]". The show's [[The Simpsons opening sequence|opening sequence]], and various scenes of band practice suggests that Milhouse plays a brass or woodwind instrument, possibly clarinet or trumpet, but all the Springfield Elementary band members, besides Lisa, are very poor musicians. Milhouse is allergic to honey, [[wheat]], [[dairy product|dairy]], mistletoe, holly, the red parts of candy canes, and his own tears. === Romance === Milhouse harbors an occasionally reciprocated crush on Lisa, but their relationship is never shown as anything other than acquaintance or friendship. As shown in "[[Lisa's Date with Density]]", when she admits she liked Nelson – at the end of that episode, after she has stopped liking Nelson, Milhouse asks Lisa who will be her next crush; Lisa coyly answers that it could be anybody and Milhouse rejoices. Lisa has always opposed the idea of going out with Milhouse (e.g. "Lisa's Date with Density" and "[[Future-Drama]]"); however, in the episode "[[The Last of the Red Hat Mamas]]", after Milhouse starts tutoring Lisa in Italian and takes her to Springfield's Little Italy, she begins to develop feelings for him, until she catches him with a girl named Angelica, and began cursing in Italian and chasing him with a branch just as his grandmother had done. Milhouse's first real girlfriend was Samantha Stanky, a new student who had moved to [[Springfield (The Simpsons)|Springfield]] from [[Phoenix, Arizona]] in the episode "[[Bart's Friend Falls in Love]]".{{Cite web |last=Zachary |first=Brandon |date=February 15, 2021 |title=The Simpsons: Milhouse's One-Episode Girlfriend Deserved To Stay in Springfield |url=https://www.cbr.com/simpsons-milhouse-girlfriend-samantha-should-stay-springfield/ |access-date=April 18, 2026 |website=CBR |language=en}} After her father who responds to Bart's call caught her and Milhouse kissing, he shipped her off to a Catholic girls' school run by French-Canadian nuns. While Milhouse's official first kiss was with Samantha in the aforementioned episode, it was contradicted in the episode "[[The Way We Weren't]]", where Milhouse accidentally kisses [[Homer Simpson|Homer]], during a game of [[spin the bottle]] that Homer interrupted. In the episode "[[Homer Scissorhands]]", Milhouse dated fifth grader Taffy. The relationship ended when Milhouse and Taffy caught Lisa spying on them in the bushes. Taffy told Lisa that Milhouse still loves her, and Lisa kisses Milhouse because "he looks cute in the moonlight". Lisa told Milhouse that he should not give up searching for other girls and that life has unexpected things to offer. In the episode "[[The Bart Wants What It Wants]]", Milhouse has a romantic relationship with Greta Wolfcastle, daughter of film star Rainier Wolfcastle. Milhouse and Lisa's relationship has been used in episodes set in the show's future, outside of the show's [[canon (fiction)|canon]]. In the episode "[[Lisa's Wedding]]", set 15 years into the future, Milhouse is Homer's boss at the nuclear plant, and after learning of Lisa's impending marriage, Milhouse recalls an earlier date with Lisa in which she said she might never marry, then angrily prepares Homer's annual review. Later in the episode, Lisa wonders if it is acceptable to wear a white wedding dress, suggesting that she had already lost her virginity; Marge tells her, "Milhouse doesn't count". In the episode "[[Holidays of Future Passed]]" (2011), set 30 years into the future, Lisa and Milhouse are married and have a daughter, Zia.{{cite web |url=https://screenrant.com/the-simpsons-every-possible-future-list/ |title=The Simpsons: Every Possible Future For The Family, Explained |author=Brandon Zachary|date=June 30, 2025 |website=[[Screen Rant]]}} == Creation == Milhouse was designed by [[Matt Groening]] for a planned series on [[NBC]], which was abandoned.{{cite news |last1=Venable |first1=Nick |title=The Crazy Story Behind Milhouse's Creation on The Simpsons |url=https://www.cinemablend.com/television/1591910/the-crazy-story-behind-milhouses-creation-on-the-simpsons |access-date=November 13, 2020 |publisher=Cinema Blend |date=November 30, 2016}} The design was then used for a ''[[Butterfinger]]'' commercial, and it was decided to use the character in the series.Groening, Matt. (2006). "A Bit from the Animators", illustrated commentary for "[[Lisa's Date with Density]]", in ''The Simpsons: The Complete Eighth Season'' [DVD]. 20th Century Fox.{{cite tweet |last=Silverman |first=David |user=tubatron |number=1395202081607151616 |date=19 May 2021 |title=Milhouse was a design Matt Groening had done for his never-realized NBC "Saturday morning show" - one of several characters. The name was the most "unfortunate name Matt Groening could think of for a kid". Years earlier, in a 1986 ''[[Life in Hell]]'' comic entitled "What to Name the Baby", Groening listed Milhouse as a name "no longer recommended".{{cite book|last=Groening|first=Matt|title=The Huge Book of Hell|publisher=Penguin|location=New York|date=1997|pages=54}} Milhouse is a favorite among the staff as [[Al Jean]] noted "most of the writers are more like Milhouse than Bart". '''GLaDOS''' ('''Genetic Lifeform and Disk Operating System''')<ref name="Jfvuc">{{cite news |url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2010/02/03/big-boss-of-the-day-portals-glados |title=Big Boss of the Day: ''Portal''{{'}}s GLaDOS |last=Schedeen |first=Jesse |work=[[IGN]] |date=February 2, 2010 |access-date=July 5, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170908070333/http://www.ign.com/articles/2010/02/03/big-boss-of-the-day-portals-glados |archive-date=September 8, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> is a fictional character in the video game series ''[[Portal (video game series)|Portal]]'', created by [[Erik Wolpaw]] and [[Kim Swift]], and voiced by [[Ellen McLain]]. GLaDOS is depicted in the first game as an [[artificial intelligence|artificially superintelligent]] computer system responsible for testing and maintenance in the [[Locations of Half-Life#Aperture Science Laboratories|Aperture Science]] Computer-Aided Enrichment Center in all titles. After betraying and almost killing the protagonist Chell, GLaDOS is revealed to be responsible for the desertion of the Enrichment Center after going rogue and killing the scientists who created her, before being defeated in a [[final boss (video games)|final boss fight]]. She is revived in ''Portal 2'', but then disabled by [[Wheatley (Portal)|Wheatley]], who takes control from her over the facility and betrays Chell, forcing GLaDOS to join forces with the latter after being forcibly downloaded onto a [[potato battery]] nicknamed '''PotatOS'''. Recordings by [[Cave Johnson (Portal)|Cave Johnson]] reveal GLaDOS to have been forcibly digitized from a human woman named '''Caroline'''.

The inspiration for the character's creation extends from Wolpaw's use of a [[Speech synthesis|text-to-speech]] program while writing lines for the video game ''[[Psychonauts]]''. Other [[video game developer|game developers]] working on ''Psychonauts'' found the lines funnier as a result of the synthesized voice. GLaDOS was originally intended to be present solely in the first area of ''Portal''; she was well received by other designers and her role was expanded as a result. [[Video game development#Tester|Play testers]] were motivated to complete tests in the game due to her guidance. While the game was initially designed with other characters, they were later removed, leaving GLaDOS as the only character players encounter. McLain imitated dialog read aloud by a speech synthesizer with her own voice, which was then processed to sound more robotic, and performed songs in character during the [[closing credits]] of both entries in the series. "[[Still Alive]]" became hugely successful, notably appearing in the ''[[Rock Band]]'' game series, and has been a popular song for [[YouTube]] users to [[cover version|cover]]. GLaDOS later appeared in ''[[The Lab (video game)|The Lab]]'' and ''[[Lego Dimensions]]''.

GLaDOS received critical acclaim from critics and gamers alike, citing her characterization as a variously [[narcissistic]], [[Passive-aggressive behavior|passive-aggressive]], sinister, and witty antagonist. ''[[IGN]]'' considered her one of the greatest video game characters, particularly among those created in the 2000s. Universally praised for her contributions to the caliber of ''Portal''{{'}}s narrative, GLaDOS received multiple awards for being the best new game character in 2007 from [[GameSpy]], ''[[GamePro]]'', and ''[[X-Play]]''. A number of publications listed her as one of the all-time greatest video game villains, including ''IGN'' and ''[[Game Informer]]'', both of which ranked her first. She has been the subject of significant critical analysis from both journalists and game developers, who have compared her to other villainous computer systems in fiction, including [[HAL 9000]] from ''2001: A Space Odyssey'' and [[SHODAN]] from ''[[System Shock]]'', with GLaDOS meeting the former in ''Lego Dimensions''.

==Overview==
GLaDOS operates the entirety of the Enrichment Center across most appearances, using cameras, intercoms, and other apparatus to monitor Chell as an unseen but omnipresent overseer. Her physical body is instead contained in a central circular chamber, appearing as a slender, vaguely humanoid mass of wiring and mechanical parts hanging upside-down from the ceiling. GLaDOS's main intelligence and memories are stored in a yellow-eyed ''Central Core'' forming the "head" of the assembly, with the body responsible for accessing the facility's functions, alongside attachment points for various multicolored ''personality core'' spheres to better guide or control GLaDOS's behavior. The original ''Portal'' game features the morality, intelligence, curiosity, and anger spheres underpinning her main personality, while ''Portal 2'' introduces a more independent GLaDOS, alongside the space, adventure, fact, and intelligence-dampening spheres as corrupt or rejected personality cores.{{cn|date=June 2026}}

===''Portal''===
{{Listen
|filename=Glados-welcome.ogg
|title=GLaDOS welcomes the player to the Aperture Science Enrichment Center in ''Portal''

In ''[[Portal (video game)|Portal]]'', GLaDOS is the only witness to the situation of the player character, [[Chell (Portal)|Chell]]. The game begins with GLaDOS as an unnamed computer voice introducing Chell to the game's [[Aperture Science Laboratories|Aperture Science Laboratories Enrichment Center]] and the physics of the portal gun. Her behavior is largely innocuous, though she occasionally experiences glitches and puts Chell through increasingly dangerous tests. GLaDOS uses the lure of cake and grief counseling to encourage Chell to continue,<ref name="6uiia">{{cite video game |title=Portal |developer=Valve Corporation |level=Test Chamber 15 |quote='''GLaDOS''': The Enrichment Center is committed to the well-being of all participants. Cake and grief counseling will be available at the conclusion of the test.}}</ref> only for the final test to end with a deadly fire pit. Once Chell escapes, GLaDOS's dialogue becomes increasingly erratic and personal, attempting to trick Chell into returning or accusing her of being "not a good person"<ref>{{cite video game |title=Portal |developer=Valve Corporation |level=Escape Sequence |quote='''GLaDOS''':You're not a good person. You know that, right? Good people don't end up here.}}</ref> or of breaking GLaDOS's heart by disobeying her.<ref>{{cite video game |title=Portal |developer=Valve Corporation |level=Final boss chamber |quote='''GLaDOS''':In spite of your violent behavior, the only thing you've managed to break so far is my heart}} See also the "Heartbreaker" Steam achievement for completing the final sequence</ref>

At the end of the game, after Chell moves through the bowels of the Enrichment Center, GLaDOS's chamber is reached, where the final encounter occurs. In this encounter Chell dislodges the various personality cores (each also voiced by McLain, with the exception of the final core, which is voiced in a guttural fashion by [[Mike Patton]]) and incinerates them. During the battle, it is revealed that before the events of ''Portal'', GLaDOS released a [[neurotoxin]] into the Enrichment Center, with the surviving scientists installing a morality core to prevent further incidents.<ref name="yd2Zn">{{cite video game |title=Portal |developer=Valve Corporation |level="Test Chamber 19" – Escape; GLaDOS's chamber |quote='''GLaDOS''': It was a morality core they installed after I flooded the Enrichment Center with a deadly neurotoxin to make me stop flooding the Enrichment Center with a deadly neurotoxin.}}</ref> Additionally, GLaDOS also appeals to Chell by claiming she is the only thing that can protect humanity from [[Combine (Half-Life)|"them"]].<ref name="portal-quote">{{cite video game|title=Portal|developer=Valve|publisher=Valve|date=October 9, 2007
|level="Test Chamber 19", final boss|quote='''GLaDOS''': What's going on out there will make you wish you were back in here. I have an infinite capacity for knowledge, and even I'm not sure what's going on outside. All I know is I'm the only thing standing between us and ''them''. Well, I was.}}</ref> After the cores are incinerated, the room is sucked into a vortex leading to the surface and GLaDOS is destroyed.<ref name="chamber19">{{cite video game |title=Portal |developer=Valve Corporation |date=October 10, 2007 |level=Test Chamber 19}}</ref>

===''Lab Rat''===
GLaDOS also appears as the antagonist of the ''Lab Rat'' [[webcomic]], depicting both her creation and eventual defeat from the perspective of Doug Rattmann, the last surviving Aperture employee. Rattmann worked on GLaDOS alongside another scientist named Henry. She proves to be extremely hostile to humans even in her early iterations, only operating for fractions of a [[picosecond]] before going rogue and triggering a [[AI killswitch|killswitch]]. After the morality core prevents her from killing the scientists outright, she instead conscripts all employees into mandatory testing to kill them. Rattmann ends up as the sole survivor after escaping her for several weeks, eventually managing to orchestrate the events of ''Portal'' by relisting Chell as the next test subject.{{cn|date=June 2026}}

===''Portal 2''===
In ''[[Portal 2]]'', GLaDOS initially resumes her role as test monitor in a now-ruined facility after Chell and [[Wheatley (Portal)|Wheatley]] inadvertently reactivate her. This time, she makes no attempt to hide her contempt and hatred for Chell; partly because Chell destroyed her, and partly because her quicksave system has forced her to relive her death over and over since her deactivation.<ref name="p2chapter2">{{cite video game |title=Portal 2 |developer=Valve Corporation |date=April 19, 2011 |level=Chapter 2: The Cold Boot}}</ref><ref name="p2chapter3">{{cite video game |title=Portal 2 |developer=Valve Corporation |date=April 19, 2011 |level=Chapter 3: The Return}}</ref><ref name="p2chapter4">{{cite video game |title=Portal 2 |developer=Valve Corporation |date=April 19, 2011 |level=Chapter 4: The Surprise}}</ref> Soon after she repairs the facility, Wheatley convinces Chell to perform a core transfer, putting him in charge of the facility in place of GLaDOS. At this point, he immediately becomes power-mad and puts GLaDOS into a [[Lemon battery#Variations|potato battery]], after which she reveals that Wheatley was designed with the purpose of hindering GLaDOS' decision-making process by constantly producing only bad ideas. He then betrays Chell and slams the elevator they are in, sending both her and GLaDOS into the bowels of the facility.<ref name="p2chapter5">{{cite video game |title=Portal 2 |developer=Valve Corporation |date=April 19, 2011 |level=Chapter 5: The Escape}}</ref> GLaDOS is kidnapped by a bird and later retrieved by Chell, who teams up with GLaDOS to escape from the facility. Her potato battery form then accompanies and speaks to the player directly after being skewered onto one of the prongs of Chell's portal gun. While they are escaping from the old testing facility, GLaDOS discovers that her personality originally came from an assistant to former Aperture CEO [[Cave Johnson (Portal)|Cave Johnson]] named Caroline, who was later uploaded into the GLaDOS program (it is suggested that this might have been done against her will at Cave Johnson's urging).<ref name="p2chapter6">{{cite video game |title=Portal 2 |developer=Valve Corporation |date=April 19, 2011 |level=Chapter 6: The Fall}}</ref><ref name="p2chapter7">{{cite video game |title=Portal 2 |developer=Valve Corporation |date=April 19, 2011 |level=Chapter 7: The Reunion}}</ref> After surviving Wheatley's various attempts to murder them, the two manage to corrupt him enough to perform another core transfer, but the effort is sabotaged by Wheatley. Through a collapsing ceiling, Chell shoots a portal onto the Moon, which sucks the chamber into space and leaves Chell and Wheatley dangling on the Moon surface. GLaDOS used the opportunity to regain control of the facility, knocking Wheatley away into space and saving Chell. GLaDOS reveals she felt relief for her safety but realizes that Caroline lives in her through emotion and immediately deletes her, reverting GLaDOS to her old self. Nevertheless, she decides that it is in her best interest to release Chell, as GLaDOS learned that the best solution is usually the easiest one, and felt that killing Chell would be too hard.<ref name="p2chapter9">{{cite video game |title=Portal 2 |developer=Valve Corporation |date=April 19, 2011 |level=Chapter 9: The Part Where He Kills You}}</ref>

==Development history==
Before development of GLaDOS had begun, [[Erik Wolpaw]] was writing the script for the video game ''[[Psychonauts]]'', where he went around the office, finding people to provide voices to the words until they could add the final voices to the game. Once he ran out of people, however, he began using a text-to-speech program. According to Wolpaw, people found the lines funnier than they were worth. He commented that, "no amount of writing is funnier than this text-to-speech thing reading it."<ref name="valve creative process" /> He became bitter about that, stating that he would leverage this and use it to his advantage.<ref name="valve creative process">{{cite web |last=Graft |first=Kris |url=https://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/4151/valves_writers_and_the_creative_.php?page=1 |title=Valve's Writers And The Creative Process |publisher=[[Gamasutra]] |date=November 2, 2009 |access-date=November 2, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091105201542/http://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/4151/valves_writers_and_the_creative_.php?page=1 |archive-date=November 5, 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Portal ===
[[File:GLaDOS concept art.jpg|thumb|GLaDOS went through several redesigns before artists settled on the final anthropomorphic shape. Early concepts featured a floating brain and a spider-like appearance.<ref name="primaguide" />]] [[File:Sandro Botticelli - La nascita di Venere - Google Art Project - edited.jpg|thumb|''[[The Birth of Venus]]'' was the inspiration for one design of GLaDOS, where GLaDOS's physical appearance was similar to the Roman goddess [[Venus (mythology)|Venus]], but upside down.<ref name="primaguide" />|251x251px]]''Portal'' had been under development for about a year, at a state where there were only test chambers that the player moved between. Valve found from playtesting that while players had fun with the game's concept, they were left asking of what these puzzles were leading towards.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.gamesradar.com/glados-was-added-to-portal-because-playtesters-kept-asking-when-does-the-game-start/|title=GlaDOS was added to Portal because playtesters kept asking 'When does the game start?'|first=Conner|last=Sheridan|work=[[GamesRadar]]|date=March 23, 2021|access-date=February 17, 2023|archive-date=February 17, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230217231252/https://www.gamesradar.com/glados-was-added-to-portal-because-playtesters-kept-asking-when-does-the-game-start/|url-status=live}}</ref> The team worked to come up with some type of narrative, coming down to creating an antagonist that would guide the player in early part of the game but become the goal that the player would strive for by the end.<ref name="ydPoq">{{cite web |url=http://www.pcgamer.com/valve-reflects-on-the-orange-box-ten-years-later/ |title=Valve reflects on The Orange Box, ten years later |first=Samuel |last=Roberts |date=October 10, 2017 |access-date=October 10, 2017 |work=[[PC Gamer]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171010144020/http://www.pcgamer.com/valve-reflects-on-the-orange-box-ten-years-later/ |archive-date=October 10, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> The creation of GLaDOS to serve this purpose began with a discussion between the Valve team and Wolpaw on the narrative constraints they had to deal with.<ref name="valve creative process" /> When they were designing the game, they found that they did not have enough time or staffing to use human characters, due to the amount of animation work and scene choreography involved.<ref name="valve creative process" />

A week later, to alleviate this problem, Wolpaw returned with sample dialogue made with a text-to-speech program, which was intended to be used as a series of messages relayed to the player in the relaxation vault, the first area of the game. The team liked the voice, describing it as "funny and sinister", so Wolpaw decided to add this voice to other test chambers, all the while trying to think of story elements. The developers noticed that play testers were more motivated by the voice because they became attached to it. As a result, the team decided to make GLaDOS the narrative voice of ''Portal''.<ref name="erik">{{cite web |title=Exclusive: Inside The Making Of Portal |url=http://www.gamasutra.com/php-bin/news_index.php?story=16885 |publisher=[[Gamasutra]] |access-date=August 25, 2009 |date=January 10, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100509140022/http://www.gamasutra.com/php-bin/news_index.php?story=16885 |archive-date=May 9, 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref> While designing GLaDOS, one of the rules that the writers had was that they would not make her seem like a computer, for example having her say, "Oh my nuts and bolts." While GLaDOS is physically a computer and speaks with a computerized voice, they intended her to speak to the player-character like a regular person.<ref name="valve creative process" />

GLaDOS's physical appearance went through several iterations when Valve had [[Jason Brashill]] help drive the visual creation of GLaDOS. Early designs used for her included a floating brain, a spider-like appearance, and an upside-down version of [[Sandro Botticelli]]'s painting ''[[The Birth of Venus]]'' with the four personality cores around her body.<ref name="primaguide">{{cite book |title=Half-Life 2: The Orange Box: Prima Official Game Guide |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pXO7CiGvAoIC |last1=Hodgson |first1=David S. J. |last2=Stratton |first2=Stephen |last3=Lopez |first3=Miguel |publisher=Random House Digital, Inc. |year=2007 |pages=217, 266, 267, 268 |isbn=9780761556930 |access-date=October 15, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170119145105/https://books.google.com/books?id=pXO7CiGvAoIC |archive-date=January 19, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> Eventually, they settled on the design of the robotic figure hanging upside down. This was done to convey both a sense of raw mechanical power and femininity.<ref name="Pcom">Developer commentary, ''[[Portal (video game)|Portal]]'', [[Valve Corporation]] (2007)</ref><!--Anyone feel like grabbing the quote from the commentary?--> A large disk with the four personality cores hanging from it was added to her design, when she was still just a sphere standing above it. However, the team found it to be too small, giving her a body and putting it below the disk.<ref name="primaguide" /> Another early design was when GLaDOS was only a cube, which was used for the removed laser battle mentioned below.<ref name="kotaku_devs">{{cite web |last=McWhertor |first=Michael |url=https://www.kotaku.com.au/2008/02/portal_devs_reveal_the_glados_that_never_was_inspiration_behind_weighted_companion_cube-2/ |title=Portal Devs Reveal The GLaDOS That Never Was, Inspiration Behind Weighted Companion Cube |publisher=Kotaku |date=February 23, 2008 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170516174403/https://www.kotaku.com.au/2008/02/portal_devs_reveal_the_glados_that_never_was_inspiration_behind_weighted_companion_cube-2/ |archive-date=May 16, 2017 |url-status=usurped}}</ref> The large chamber that the player-character encounters was the result of the team wanting to build a space that brought a great deal of attention to her.<ref name="primaguide" />

GLaDOS was written with the intent of making her more understandable and empathetic to players, making her villainy more tragic. Kim Swift, team leader of ''Portal'', described her growth in the game as her becoming more and more human. The two-hour total playtime for ''Portal'' allowed the writers enough time to let players get to know GLaDOS.<ref name="erikkim">{{cite web |title=Still Alive: Kim Swift And Erik Wolpaw Talk Portal |last=Sheffield |first=Brandon |url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/business/still-alive-kim-swift-and-erik-wolpaw-talk-portal |publisher=[[Gamasutra]] |access-date=March 9, 2018 |date=March 25, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180108062729/https://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/3585/still_alive_kim_swift_and_erik_.php |archive-date=January 8, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Wolpaw commented that while GLaDOS did yell and fire rockets at the player, she fulfilled his desire for a kind of villain that has not been too overdone.<ref name="rps" /> He described her as both supportive and funny, while also sad and scared. One of his intentions was for players to believe that they are "putting her through the wringer emotionally".<ref name="rps" /> The game was designed to have a clear beginning, middle, and end. Wolpaw stated that with each new part, GLaDOS's personality changed. She begins as a supportive, yet also increasingly sinister character, where she delivers exposition about the general Aperture mindset. However, once the player-character escapes, she begins to speak in first-person singular rather than first-person plural. She shows desperation due to her lack of control at this point, adding that more emotion begins to creep through her voice. After destroying the morality core, she becomes unhinged, featuring an almost human voice. This voice, described as sultry by Wolpaw, was originally to be used for turrets, but it did not work out. Because they liked it so much, they chose to use it for GLaDOS.<ref name="rps">{{cite web |last=Walker |first=John |url=http://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2007/10/31/rps-interview-valves-erik-wolpaw/ |title=RPS Interview: Valve's Erik Wolpaw |website=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]] |date=October 31, 2007 |access-date=August 18, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100827184326/http://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2007/10/31/rps-interview-valves-erik-wolpaw/ |archive-date=August 27, 2010 |url-status=live}}</ref>

==== Final battle ====
In designing the final "encounter" with GLaDOS in ''Portal'', one of the important aspects to it was giving the players a predisposition to the [[Weighted Companion Cube]], an object that GLaDOS gives to the player-character and tells her to protect. This was accomplished by forcing the player to incinerate it, therein providing a tutorial for how to defeat the boss and an angle of personal revenge for Chell. GLaDOS was originally designed to be a devious boss, citing one form where she would use a series of lasers, like those seen in ''[[James Bond]]'' films. However, it was determined that this [[twitch gameplay]] distracted players from GLaDOS, and was too different from the game's puzzle-solving gameplay. Additionally, it was difficult for players to detect when they were hit, so the developers switched the gameplay to feature rockets. This incarnation of the final boss was dubbed "Portal Kombat", which Swift describes as a "high intensity rocket battle".<ref name="success">{{cite web |last=Kumar |first=Matthew |date=February 27, 2008 |title=Best Of GDC: The Secrets Of Portal's Huge Success |url=https://www.gamasutra.com/php-bin/news_index.php?story=17625 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180108062757/https://www.gamasutra.com/php-bin/news_index.php?story=17625 |archive-date=January 8, 2018 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |publisher=[[Gamasutra]]}}</ref> However, Wolpaw disliked it because no one was paying attention to what GLaDOS was saying. While it went over well with hardcore shooter fans, the people who liked the puzzle-focused gameplay were turned off by it. The third boss was a chase scene, with players pursuing GLaDOS down a corridor. Wolpaw sharply criticized the pacing, which caused the players to wander around until they found the corridor, at which point a series of pistons would spring out of the walls.<ref name="success" />

The developers came to the conclusion that complex battles would only serve to confuse players. One play tester helped them by pointing out the quality of the fire pit puzzle, a puzzle that has the player-character riding on a moving platform that is descending into flames, requiring players to find a way to survive. He stated that it was both dramatic and exciting, but also a difficult puzzle. Wolpaw stated that this made no sense, commenting that it was one of the easiest puzzles in the game. He added that the battle was a dramatic high-point, since it was the first time GLaDOS directly tries to kill the player-character and the first time that players have to use the environment to their advantage. After learning about what fellow Valve developers had planned for the final boss battle in ''Half-Life 2: Episode Two'', the Portal developers decided to implement a neurotoxin that would kill the player-character in six minutes.<ref name="kotaku_devs" /> This made it easier on the writers, who only had to write six minutes of dialogue. As a result, they scaled the game back, intending to ensure that everyone was able to see the game to the very end.<ref name="success" />

=== Portal 2 ===
Erik Wolpaw and [[Jay Pinkerton]] were mainly responsible for the [[Single-player video game|single-player]] campaign's story, while [[Chet Faliszek]] focused on the lines for GLaDOS in the cooperative campaign.<ref name="eginterview">{{cite web |last=Welsh |first=Oli |date=April 25, 2011 |title=Portal 2: "Let's make Caddyshack" Interview - Page 2 |url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-04-24-portal-2-lets-make-caddyshack-interview?page=2 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171229231743/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-04-24-portal-2-lets-make-caddyshack-interview?page=2 |archive-date=December 29, 2017 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |publisher=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref> ''Portal 2'' was originally not intended to feature GLaDOS or Chell, the player-character from ''Portal''. However, the demand for all of these to be implemented into ''Portal 2'' was great enough that they chose to do so. Originally, the character Cave Johnson was intended to be the antagonist instead and ''Portal 2'' to be a prequel.<ref name="rps2">{{cite web |last=Walker |first=John |date=April 27, 2011 |title=Valve On Portal 2: Spoiler Interview Part One |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2011/04/27/valve-on-portal-2-spoiler-interview-part-one/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215000445/https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2011/04/27/valve-on-portal-2-spoiler-interview-part-one/ |archive-date=December 15, 2017 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |website=[[Rock Paper Shotgun]]}}</ref> Before implementing Chell, they considered introducing a new player-character who would at one point inadvertently reactivate GLaDOS.<ref name="ulPce">{{cite web |last=Welsh |first=Oli |date=April 25, 2011 |title=Portal 2: "Let's make Caddyshack" Interview |url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-04-24-portal-2-lets-make-caddyshack-interview |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110428041701/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-04-24-portal-2-lets-make-caddyshack-interview |archive-date=April 28, 2011 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |publisher=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref> During play testing, Wolpaw found that there were two groups that opposed each other: One group was excited to see GLaDOS return, while the other did not want to wake her up and questioned why players would want to do that. As such, the character Wheatley was introduced, who inadvertently wakes GLaDOS while trying to escape the facility with Chell. Wheatley and GLaDOS served as a contrast to each other; where GLaDOS has a more cold, machine-sounding voice due to her intelligence, Wheatley sounds incredibly human due to his lack of it.<ref name="eginterview" /> Play testers were also bothered by the fact that the new protagonist was not recognized by GLaDOS when she awoke; as such, they changed the new character back into Chell.<ref name="GAGjo">{{cite web |last=yin-Poole |first=Wesley |date=March 14, 2011 |title=How Valve Opened Up Portal 2 Interview - Page 2 |url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-03-10-portal-2-how-valve-opened-up-portal-2?page=2 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180308104105/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-03-10-portal-2-how-valve-opened-up-portal-2?page=2 |archive-date=March 8, 2018 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |publisher=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref> Wolpaw and the designers were not sure what to do with GLaDOS and were wary to do the same thing as the last game. They felt that she should "go someplace", and that since GLaDOS is considered somewhat charming in the first game and players enjoyed being with her, they would utilize Wheatley as a different, external threat.<ref name="eginterview" /> In the early part of the game, GLaDOS introduces each chamber and congratulates the player on completing it; though they could have included intermediate dialog from GLaDOS while the player attempts to solve each chamber, they found this would be distracting to players and limited her presence in the game to only these points.<ref name="gi p2 testchamber">{{cite magazine |last=Reeves |first=Ben |date=March 17, 2010 |title=Thinking With Portals: Making a ''Portal 2'' Test Chamber |url=https://gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2010/03/17/thinking-with-portals-making-a-test-chamber.aspx |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111223151107/http://www.gameinformer.com/b/features/archive/2010/03/17/thinking-with-portals-making-a-test-chamber.aspx |archive-date=December 23, 2011 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |magazine=[[Game Informer]]}}</ref>

The developers considered having GLaDOS and Chell act more like a "buddy cop" duo, but felt that since Chell never talked, it would not work. He compared her transformation into a potato and having her power stripped away to the game ''[[Jenga]]'': "You're taking stuff off the bottom and seeing what happens." While she was in the potato form, the designers noticed a great difference between the intimidating, all-powerful GLaDOS talking to you, and the more powerless GLaDOS that's attached to your gun. They found that playtesters were not interested in her when she was powerless and insulting players, and would question why they were having to carry this character with them. They decided to give her a personality shift and become Chell's sidekick on the basis that players would not tolerate her constantly harassing them. To keep players from feeling that they should want to abandon GLaDOS in her powerless form to prevent her from becoming powerful again, the designers made sure to give players a reason to bring her with them.<ref name="rps2" /> In considering the interaction between Chell and GLaDOS, Erik Johnson compared GLaDOS to a "jealous ex-girlfriend", noting that Chell is "the only person she can have interaction with, but the problem is her only way of interacting with anyone is to test them".<ref name="gamasutra johnson interview">{{cite web |last=Sheffield |first=Brandon |date=November 8, 2010 |title=Rewarding The Players: Valve On Portal 2 |url=https://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/6198/rewarding_the_players_valve_on_.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215054200/https://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/6198/rewarding_the_players_valve_on_.php |archive-date=December 15, 2017 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |publisher=[[Gamasutra]]}}</ref> While they introduced new characters into the game, the focus of the story in ''Portal 2'' remained the connection and interaction between Chell and GLaDOS, and focuses more on the fallout from Chell's destruction of GLaDOS from the first game.<ref name="gamasutra wolpaw interview">{{cite web |last=Remo |first=Chris |date=September 20, 2010 |title=Synthesizing Portal 2 |url=https://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/6141/synthesizing_portal_2.php |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309182822/https://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/6141/synthesizing_portal_2.php |archive-date=March 9, 2018 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |publisher=Gamasutra}}</ref>

The cooperative campaign contains a separate story between the two robotic characters and GLaDOS. The cooperative campaign includes additional dialog from GLaDOS; the original dialogue Wolpaw wrote for GLaDOS was made for two human women, Chell and a new character named "Mel", with the assumption of image issues; but this dialog remains in place even after the change of the co-op characters to robots.<ref name="joystiq portal co-op">{{cite web |last=Grant |first=Christopher |date=June 21, 2010 |title=Preview: Portal 2 (co-op) |url=https://www.engadget.com/2010/06/21/preview-portal-2-co-op/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180104192705/https://www.engadget.com/2010/06/21/preview-portal-2-co-op/ |archive-date=January 4, 2018 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |work=[[Engadget]]}}</ref> The dialog written for GLaDOS in the co-operative campaign is aimed to try to break the bond between the two robot characters. Valve initially considered having separate lines for GLaDOS that would be given to each player individually, but found this to be a significant effort for minimal benefit. The writers also attempted adding GLaDOS lines that would make the players attempt to compete against each other, such as the awarding of meaningless points, but playtesters did not respond well to these lines.<ref name="pcgamer interview">{{cite web |last=Francis |first=Tom |date=September 10, 2010 |title=Interview: Valve on their insane Portal 2 ideas |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/interview-valve-on-their-insane-portal-2-ideas/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309120412/https://www.pcgamer.com/interview-valve-on-their-insane-portal-2-ideas/ |archive-date=March 9, 2018 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |work=[[PC World (magazine)|PC World]]}}</ref>

The writers found they needed another character to play off of Cave during his recordings; instead of hiring a voice actor for a few lines, they economized by reusing McLain to play Caroline, Cave's assistant.<ref name="pcgamer wolpaw interview">{{cite web |last=Stanton |first=Rich |date=April 26, 2011 |title=Erik Wolpaw on Portal 2's ending: "the [spoiler] is probably lurking out there somewhere" |url=https://www.pcgamer.com/erik-wolpaw-on-portal-2s-ending-the-spoiler-is-probably-lurking-out-there-somewhere/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309120321/https://www.pcgamer.com/erik-wolpaw-on-portal-2s-ending-the-spoiler-is-probably-lurking-out-there-somewhere/ |archive-date=March 9, 2018 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |work=[[PC Gamer]]}}</ref> This led naturally to providing a backstory for the creation of GLaDOS, who is revealed in-game to be based on Caroline's personality.<ref name="Portal 2">{{cite video game |title=Portal 2 |developer=Valve Corporation |date=April 19, 2011 |platform=Microsoft Windows |scene=Chapter 7 |level=Speed Ramp |people=Dario Casali}}</ref> This later led the writers to develop a full story arc for GLaDOS where she would come to recall her past, learn from it to solve the dilemma, and then subsequently delete it and reset herself.<ref name="eurogamer wolpaw interview">{{cite web |last=Welch |first=Oli |date=April 25, 2011 |title=Portal 2: "Let's make Caddyshack" |url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-04-24-portal-2-lets-make-caddyshack-interview |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110428041701/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-04-24-portal-2-lets-make-caddyshack-interview |archive-date=April 28, 2011 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |publisher=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref> The designers wanted to start GLaDOS's role in ''Portal 2'' off with her being incredibly upset with Chell. They felt however that this concept would quickly feel redundant if they did not put her "into another space". They accomplished this through a combination of her anger with Wheatley and her conflict with her past life as Caroline. Through the course of the game's events, GLaDOS's personality shifts significantly; however, at the end, she reverts to her original personality, an action Wolpaw sums up as explicitly rejecting her change and saying "You know what? Done." While they wanted to give players the sense that they had defeated GLaDOS, they felt that they should not have players fight her as a boss battle; as a result, they had her let Chell go due to the reasoning that Chell was too difficult for her to handle.<ref name="5Dk8r">{{cite web |last=Welsh |first=Oli |date=April 25, 2011 |title=Portal 2: "Let's make Caddyshack" Interview - Page 3 |url=http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-04-24-portal-2-lets-make-caddyshack-interview?page=3 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180121072058/http://www.eurogamer.net/articles/2011-04-24-portal-2-lets-make-caddyshack-interview?page=3 |archive-date=January 21, 2018 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |publisher=[[Eurogamer]]}}</ref> Writer Jay Pinkerton stated that GLaDOS was an exemplification of a villain who can go from tender to villainous, and that "she's not just this moustache-twirling villain". He also stated that she has a passive-aggressive nature and will never directly attack but instead use "subtle mind games". The designers also intended to make it vague whether or not GLaDOS was under the control of the machine that she was attached to.<ref name="rps2" /> Wolpaw also specifically called her passive-aggressive alongside mildly sarcastic, and compared her to ''[[The Sopranos]]'' character [[Livia Soprano]].<ref name="news.com.au interview">{{cite news |last=Ramadge |first=Andrew |date=February 22, 2011 |title=GLaDOS, the greatest video game villain of all time, is back for more cake and chaos in Portal 2 |url=http://www.news.com.au/technology/home-entertainment/glados-the-greatest-video-game-villain-of-all-time-back-for-cake-and-chaos-in-portal-2/news-story/4d7c1cfb59654c53e067f8cb2e78f939 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215070145/http://www.news.com.au/technology/home-entertainment/glados-the-greatest-video-game-villain-of-all-time-back-for-cake-and-chaos-in-portal-2/news-story/4d7c1cfb59654c53e067f8cb2e78f939 |archive-date=December 15, 2017 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |publisher=[[News.com.au]]}}</ref>

=== Voice design ===
[[File:Ellen McLain by Gage Skidmore.jpg|thumb|GLaDOS is voiced by actress [[Ellen McLain]].]]
In creating the voice for GLaDOS, voice actress [[Ellen McLain]] attempted to sound like a computer. This was accomplished by her emulating a computer-generated voice that the Valve team played for her and her adding emotion to lines when appropriate.<ref name="mclain">{{cite web |title=GLaDOS Speaks |last=Hatfield |first=Daemon |url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2007/11/01/glados-speaks |publisher=IGN |access-date=March 9, 2018 |date=October 31, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180228023103/http://www.ign.com/articles/2007/11/01/glados-speaks |archive-date=February 28, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> While designing her voice, Swift commented that it was difficult to write some of the lines for GLaDOS, describing McLain as "super likable", and that they should write for that.<ref name="erikkim" /> She also performed the song "[[Still Alive]]", which features GLaDOS singing to the effect that she is still alive by the end of ''Portal''. This song was written by [[Jonathan Coulton]], who was approached by the team and asked if he would want to write a song for them. He later decided that it would be a good idea to do a song featuring one of the voices from the game that would tie up the story at the end.<ref name="jonathanblog">{{cite web |last=Coulton |first=Jonathan |title=Portal: The Skinny |url=https://www.jonathancoulton.com/2007/10/15/portal-the-skinny/ |access-date=March 9, 2018 |date=October 15, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171201132235/https://www.jonathancoulton.com/2007/10/15/portal-the-skinny/ |archive-date=December 1, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> Swift stated that the team wanted the players to leave the game happy, leading to them implementing the song in the first place. Wolpaw and the other writers wrote down a list of things that would make people happy, which resulted in "Still Alive".<ref name="success" /> In discussing the difficulties in singing the song as GLaDOS, McLain listed one of the difficulties as breathing, because computers do not need to breathe. As a result, she had to sing the phrases in one breath, while attempting to keep a clean, even tone.<ref name="thegamingliberty.com interview">{{cite web |last=Murphy |first=Denis |title=An interview with Ellen McLain and John Patrick Lowrie |url=http://thegamingliberty.com/index.php/2010/07/29/an-interview-with-ellen-mclain-and-john-patrick-lowrie/ |access-date=May 11, 2011 |date=July 29, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110427012317/http://thegamingliberty.com/index.php/2010/07/29/an-interview-with-ellen-mclain-and-john-patrick-lowrie |archive-date=April 27, 2011}}</ref> Swift commented in an interview that one of the focuses of developing the game was for players to hear GLaDOS and hear her song.<ref name="Akcba">{{cite news |title=Student Union |newspaper=MCV/Develop |url=http://www.develop-online.net/features/152/Student-Union |publisher=Develop Online |access-date=August 24, 2009 |date=March 18, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091214103714/http://www.develop-online.net/features/152/Student-Union |archive-date=December 14, 2009}}</ref>

GLaDOS continues to be voiced by McLain in ''Portal 2'', who worked with Valve every two weeks to record the majority of the dialogue for the game.<ref name="news.com.au interview" /> The frequency of her voice sessions allowed Valve to experiment with GLaDOS's lines and how they came out within the final game.<ref name="news.com.au interview" /> After finding that "Still Alive" was a large part of ''Portal''{{'s}} success, Valve included more music in ''Portal 2'', including further involvement from Coulton.<ref name="gi reveal">{{cite magazine |title=Portal 2 |first=Meagan |last=VanBurkleo |date=April 2010 |pages=50–62 |magazine=[[Game Informer]]}}</ref> Coulton wrote a new song for the game's ending credits, "Want You Gone", which is written from GLaDOS's viewpoint of wanting to rid herself of Chell. It is performed by McLain.<ref name="ZYL9e">{{cite web |url=http://www.g4tv.com/thefeed/blog/post/712014/portal-2-ending-song-want-you-gone-by-jonathan-coulton-video-and-lyrics/ |title=Portal 2 Ending Song: Want You Gone by Jonathan Coulton Video and Lyrics |first=Dana |last=Vinson |date=April 20, 2011 |access-date=April 21, 2011 |publisher=[[G4 (U.S. TV channel)|G4 TV]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121017092218/http://www.g4tv.com/thefeed/blog/post/712014/portal-2-ending-song-want-you-gone-by-jonathan-coulton-video-and-lyrics/ |archive-date=October 17, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref> McLain wrote "GLaDOS' Song", her only composition, offering it to Valve for use in the game; it was not used, though she and [[John Patrick Lowrie|John Lowrie]] performed it for ''[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]]''.<ref name="vice-profile">{{cite web |url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/glados-and-the-sniper/ |title=GLaDOS and The Sniper: A Voice Acting Love Story |date=March 30, 2015 |access-date=February 17, 2023|work=[[Vice (magazine)|Vice]] |first=Jagger |last=Gravning|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220922021326/https://www.vice.com/en/article/78xdgg/glados-and-the-sniper|archive-date=September 22, 2022|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="glados-song-youtube">{{cite AV media |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hgiNKEXtx7I |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/hgiNKEXtx7I |archive-date=December 21, 2021 |url-status=live |people=John Lowrie, Ellen McLain |date=April 7, 2015 |title=GLaDOS' Song |medium=YouTube |language=en |quote=This is a song that Ellen wrote as an easter egg for Portal 2. It was never used, but when Jagger Gravning heard it when he was interviewing us for a profile on Vice Magazine he took us into the studio to record it.}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

===Use in promotion===
{{see also|Potato Sack}}
[[File:Gdc2010 newell portal BSOD.jpg|thumb|As part of the [[alternate reality game]] related to ''Portal 2''{{'}}s announcement at the 2010 [[Game Developers Conference]], Valve produced a [[blue screen of death]] which features GLaDOS's name in place of the [[Microsoft Windows|Windows]] name.<ref name="portalbsod_gdc" />]]
GLaDOS has been used several times for reveals in the ''Portal'' series. At E3 2008, GLaDOS's voice was utilized to reveal the ''Portal'' expansion ''Portal: Still Alive''.<ref name="CL9xE">{{cite news |last=Molina |first=Brett |url=http://content.usatoday.com/communities/technologylive/post/2008/07/52683320/1 |newspaper=[[USA Today]] |title=E3 2008: Inside Microsoft's press briefing |date=July 14, 2008 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121008085711/http://content.usatoday.com/communities/technologylive/post/2008/07/52683320/1 |archive-date=October 8, 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref> She has also been used to show ''Portal 2'' reveals; initially, a [[blue screen of death]] image was used instead of a revelation of ''Portal 2'', showing the typical text found in a blue screen of death, but with GLaDOS's name at the top.<ref name="portalbsod_gdc">{{cite web |last=Plunkett |first=Luke |url=https://kotaku.com/portal-2-hijacks-blue-screen-of-death-at-gdc-awards-5491651 |title=Portal 2 Hijacks Blue Screen of Death At GDC Awards |publisher=Kotaku |date=March 12, 2010 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171215053715/https://kotaku.com/5491651/portal-2-hijacks-blue-screen-of-death-at-gdc-awards |archive-date=December 15, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> In the reveal of the [[PlayStation 3]] version of ''Portal 2'', GLaDOS's voice was used to introduce [[Gabe Newell]], the co-founder of Valve at [[E3 2010]], where he revealed ''Portal 2'' for the PlayStation 3.<ref name="final hours">{{cite book |asin=B004XMZZKQ |title=The Final Hours of Portal 2 |chapter=10: Making Games is Hard |first=Geoff |last=Keighley |year=2011}} Also available as iPad or Steam application.</ref> ''Portal 2''{{'}}s release was preceded by a collection of video games in a collection called ''[[Potato Sack]]'', which featured thirteen independently developed games. These games were all a part of an alternate reality, based on a cryptic narrative that suggested the awakening and relaunch of GLaDOS. Valve provided the developers access to their art assets to include ''Portal 2''-themed content into them, and in some cases, McLain recorded new dialog specifically for these games. The alternate reality game ultimately led to "GLaDOS@Home", a [[distributed computing]] spoof, which prompted players to play the independently developed games to awaken GLaDOS ahead of schedule, effectively promoting the Steam release of ''Portal 2'' about 10 hours earlier than the official time.<ref name="AuIuy">{{cite news |url=http://www.gamepro.com/article/news/218877/play-indie-games-help-portal-2-release-early/ |title=Play indie games, help Portal 2 release early |first=Pete |last=Davidson |date=April 15, 2011 |access-date=April 15, 2011 |publisher=[[GamePro]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111203050324/http://www.gamepro.com/article/news/218877/play-indie-games-help-portal-2-release-early/ |archive-date=December 3, 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="c34u3">{{cite magazine |url=https://www.wired.com/gamelife/2011/04/portal-2-early-launch/ |title=Play Steam Games, Launch Portal 2 Early |first=Jason |last=Schreier |date=April 15, 2011 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |magazine=[[Wired (magazine)|Wired]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110418184148/http://www.wired.com/gamelife/2011/04/portal-2-early-launch |archive-date=April 18, 2011 |url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Jonathan Coulton cropped.jpg|thumb|[[Jonathan Coulton]] received significant attention for his composition of the credits song "[[Still Alive]]".]]
The song "Still Alive" has garnered significant attention from fans and critics alike. It was released as a part of ''[[The Orange Box#Soundtrack|The Orange Box Official Soundtrack]]'' and appeared in other video games, including the ''[[Rock Band]]'' series and ''[[Left 4 Dead 2]]'', the latter which was also released by Valve. The song has been performed in multiple venues by Jonathan Coulton which includes the [[PAX (event)|Penny Arcade Expo]] in 2008, the [[Press Start: Symphony of Games|Press Start -Symphony of Games-]] concert in 2009, and the [[Game Developers Conference]] in 2008.<ref name="IF3Vt">{{cite web |url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2008/02/29/game-audio-network-guild-announces-award-winners-for-6th-annual-gang-awards |title=Game Audio Network Guild Announces Award Winners for 6th Annual G.A.N.G. In 2020, GLaDOS became one of the featured voices on [[15.ai]], a [[generative AI]] text-to-speech [[web application]] that allowed users to generate speech in the voices of fictional characters.<ref name="Zwiezen-2021">{{cite web|url=https://www.kotaku.com.au/2021/01/this-website-lets-you-make-glados-say-whatever-you-want/|title=This Website Lets You Make GLaDOS Say Whatever You Want|first=Zack|last=Zwiezen|work=[[Kotaku Australia]]|date=January 18, 2021|access-date=February 17, 2023|archive-date=February 17, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230217231907/https://www.kotaku.com.au/2021/01/this-website-lets-you-make-glados-say-whatever-you-want/|url-status=usurped}}</ref><ref name="QQ">{{cite web |last=新智元 |date=March 15, 2020|title=模型参数过亿跑不动?看MIT小哥, 少量数据完成高质量文本转语音!|url=https://news.qq.com/rain/a/20200315A0B0AY00|access-date=February 22, 2025|website=[[QQ News]]}}</ref>  The service gained widespread popularity in early 2021, with GLaDOS's voice being particularly well-received by users. According to reports, the AI reproduction of GLaDOS's mechanical voice was so convincing that some listeners mistook it for new recordings by Ellen McLain.<ref name="Zwiezen-2021"/> Fans created original content featuring GLaDOS using 15.ai, ranging from humorous [[Internet meme|memes]] to [[crossover (fiction)|crossover content]] with other franchises.<ref name="Ruppert2021">{{cite magazine |last=Ruppert |first=Liana |date=January 18, 2021 |title=Make Portal's GLaDOS And Other Beloved Characters Say The Weirdest Things With This App |url=https://www.gameinformer.com/gamer-culture/2021/01/18/make-portals-glados-and-other-beloved-characters-say-the-weirdest-things |magazine=[[Game Informer]]}}</ref><ref name="Morton2021">{{cite web |last=Morton |first=Lauren |date=January 18, 2021 |title=Put words in game characters' mouths with this fascinating text to speech tool |url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2021/01/18/put-words-in-game-characters-mouths-with-this-fascinating-text-to-speech-tool/ |website=[[Rock, Paper, Shotgun]]}}</ref> Some users used [[Voice user interface|voice command software]] to create [[personal assistants]] in the voice of GLaDOS.<ref>{{cite web |last=Yoshiyuki |first=Furushima |date=January 18, 2021 |title=「Portal」のGLaDOSや「UNDERTALE」のサンズがテキストを読み上げてくれる.文章に込められた感情まで再現することを目指すサービス「15.ai」が話題に |trans-title=Portal's GLaDOS and UNDERTALE's Sans Will Read Text for You. "15.ai" Service Aims to Reproduce Even the Emotions in Text, Becomes Topic of Discussion |url=https://news.denfaminicogamer.jp/news/210118f |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210118051321/https://news.denfaminicogamer.jp/news/210118f |archive-date=January 18, 2021 |access-date=December 18, 2024 |website=[[:ja:電ファミニコゲーマー|Den Fami Nico Gamer]] |language=ja}}</ref>

The game ''[[Death Stranding]]'', paying homage to [[Valve Corporation]], features a character GLaDOS, who only communicates via email and through aliases. Death Stranding's GLaDOS provides side quests to collect cubes, resulting in the player being rewarded with Valve-themed gear. Near the end of the game, GLaDOS reveals herself and confesses that she does not belong to the world of Death Stranding, and showed up there only to conduct experiments. Finally, GLaDOS returns to her own world.<ref name="deathstranding">{{cite web|url=https://explosionnetwork.com/articles/death-stranding-half-life-portal-missions-guide-locations|title=Death Stranding - Half-Life & Portal Missions Guide & Locations|first=Dylan|last=Blight|website=explosionnetwork.com|date=July 16, 2020|access-date=October 25, 2022|archive-date=October 25, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221025010215/https://explosionnetwork.com/articles/death-stranding-half-life-portal-missions-guide-locations|url-status=live}}</ref> McLain provides GLaDOS's voice as part of a side mission in ''[[Cyberpunk 2077]]'' in which the player tracks down driverless taxis.<ref name="cyberpunk-thegamer" /><ref name="cyberpunk-pcgamer" /> McLain reprised her role as GLaDOS for a [[GEICO]] commercial based on ''Portal'', released in January 2022.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.theverge.com/tldr/2022/1/12/22881121/geico-portal-ad-never-asked-for-gecko-glados |title=Geico made the Portal ad we never asked for |first=Jay |last=Peters |date=January 12, 2022 |accessdate=January 12, 2022 |work=[[The Verge]] |archive-date=January 13, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220113020001/https://www.theverge.com/tldr/2022/1/12/22881121/geico-portal-ad-never-asked-for-gecko-glados |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Reception and analysis==
Paste Magazine's Jason Killingsworth listed GLaDOS as the sixth best new character of the decade; he wrote that he considers her one of the most likable villains in video-game history and that "we only killed her because we had to".<ref name="IISdc">{{cite web |last=Killingsworth |first=Jason |url=https://www.pastemagazine.com/blogs/lists/2009/11/the-10-best-video-game-characters-of-the-decade-20.html |title=The 10 Best Video Game Characters of the Decade (2000-2009) |magazine=Paste Magazine |date=November 19, 2009 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309120432/https://www.pastemagazine.com/blogs/lists/2009/11/the-10-best-video-game-characters-of-the-decade-20.html |archive-date=March 9, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> An editor for [[GamesRadar+|GamesRadar]] also called her one of the best new characters of the decade.<ref name="9ZiAH">{{cite web |title=The 25 best new characters of the decade |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/the-25-best-new-characters-of-the-decade/ |work=[[GamesRadar+|GamesRadar]] |access-date=March 9, 2018 |date=December 29, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309120410/https://www.gamesradar.com/the-25-best-new-characters-of-the-decade/ |archive-date=March 9, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[Guinness World Records Gamer's Edition]]'' also listed GLaDOS as second in their list of top 50 Villains.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.digitalspy.com/videogames/a453360/guinness-world-records-counts-down-top-50-video-game-villains/|title=Bowser voted top of 50 video game villains|work=[[Digital Spy]]|first=Scott|last=Nichols|date=January 24, 2013|access-date=November 6, 2022|archive-date=October 19, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211019044354/https://www.digitalspy.com/videogames/a453360/guinness-world-records-counts-down-top-50-video-game-villains/|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[Epic Games]] design director [[Cliff Bleszinski]] stated that he was motivated to complete test chambers in ''Portal''. He also compared her to an ex-girlfriend who sent [[Text messaging|text message]]s that went from friendly, to aggressive, and finally to apologetic.<ref name="VP8OF">{{cite web |last=Totilo |first=Stephen |url=https://www.mtv.com/news/2456374/gears-of-war-creator-update/ |title='Gears of War' Creator Update: Slams 'Insular' Game Developers, Puts Consoles As Epic's Priority #1, Confronts Consequences Of Loving 'Zack & Wiki' |publisher=MTV |date=February 13, 2008 |access-date=August 18, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141129190207/http://multiplayerblog.mtv.com/2008/02/13/gears-of-war-creator-update/ |archive-date=November 29, 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref> GamesRadar's Justin Towell called her the third-most difficult game bad guy to kill due to [[Stockholm syndrome]], a syndrome where hostages will bond with their captors.<ref name="J6RxX">{{cite web |title=The Top 7... bad guys you didn't want to kill |first=Justin|last=Towell |date=February 11, 2008 |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/the-top-7-game-bad-guys-you-didnt-want-to-kill/ |work=[[GamesRadar]] |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309120432/https://www.gamesradar.com/the-top-7-game-bad-guys-you-didnt-want-to-kill/ |archive-date=March 9, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> IGN editor Daemon Hatfield described GLaDOS as one of the most engaging characters to appear in a video game.<ref name="mclain" /> Cinema Blend featured GLaDOS as the best character of 2007, stating that she "breathes life, emotion, and hilarity into the lab of ''Portal''."<ref name="OJOQc">{{cite web |url=https://www.cinemablend.com/games/Best-Of-2007-Top-Five-Video-Game-Characters-Part-II-8037.html |title=Best Of 2007: Top Five Video Game Characters - Part II |work=CinemaBlend |date=December 31, 2007 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180224173606/https://www.cinemablend.com/games/Best-Of-2007-Top-Five-Video-Game-Characters-Part-II-8037.html |archive-date=February 24, 2018 |url-status=dead}}</ref> GamesRadar praised ''Portal'' as having one of the best video game stories ever, citing GLaDOS as the primary reason for this. They stated that she had the most defined personality in gaming, adding that she "redefined passive-aggressive".<ref name="qsDk1">{{cite web |url=http://www.gamesradar.com/f/the-best-videogame-stories-ever/a-200804179337286093/p-4 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130124070637/http://www.gamesradar.com/f/the-best-videogame-stories-ever/a-200804179337286093/p-4 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 24, 2013 |title=The Best Videogame Stories Ever |work=[[GamesRadar]] |date=April 17, 2008 |access-date=August 10, 2010}}</ref> [[Shoot 'em up]] expert Michael Molinari cited GLaDOS as an example of a quality boss, stating that her quality stems from her appearing throughout the game, providing motivation as well as a satisfying pay-off at the end of the game.<ref name="05wah">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamedeveloper.com/design/video-game-boss-design-for-shmups |title=Michael Molinari's Blog - Video Game Boss Design For Shmups |work=[[Gamasutra]] |date=June 19, 2010 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180225064722/https://www.gamasutra.com/blogs/MichaelMolinari/20100619/5392/Video_Game_Boss_Design_For_Shmups.php |archive-date=February 25, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Editor Randy Smith commented that the battle with GLaDOS was easy, commenting that the fight was fun rather than being annoying to beat, adding that it had an "air of epicness".<ref name="FtY5q">{{cite web |url=http://www.next-gen.biz/opinion/inevitability-change |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120907090920/http://www.next-gen.biz/opinion/inevitability-change |url-status=dead |archive-date=September 7, 2012 |title=The Inevitability of Change | Edge Magazine |publisher=Next-gen.biz |date=February 3, 2009 |access-date=May 4, 2011}}</ref>

GLaDOS is frequently cited as both a quality villain and a quality computer character. IGN called her the greatest video game villain of all time, stating that while their time with her was short, she left a mark on players like no other villain has. They cited her uniqueness as being because no other players existed in the game. They also added she was more human than most video game villains.<ref name="AHs1u">{{cite web |url=http://www.ign.com/videogame-villains/1.html |title=Top 100 Videogame Villains - GLaDOS is number 1 |work=[[IGN]] |date=May 2010 |access-date=May 18, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120217030351/http://www.ign.com/videogame-villains/1.html |archive-date=February 17, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref> [[1Up Network|''1Up.com'']] editor Scott Sharkey praised her as being the best insane video game computer. He stated that not only is she the best insane computer in video games, but in films and books as well. He explains his choice by citing her eagerness to kill the player-character, but not being overt about it until the end. He also cites her feminine voice and passive-aggressive manner for his decision.<ref name="hErhN">{{cite web |title=Top 5 Insane Computers |url=http://www.1up.com/do/feature?cId=3174288 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120525001517/http://www.1up.com/do/feature?cId=3174288 |archive-date=May 25, 2012 |work=[[1Up.com]] |first=Scott |last=Sharkey|access-date=August 24, 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> In another article, he mentions how he feels more sorry for her than any other enemy, describing her as a "digital version of the most passive-aggressive girlfriend ever". He adds that he can imagine it not being easy to be a super-intelligent computer trapped in a single building.<ref name="EbbXi">{{cite web |url=http://www.1up.com/do/feature?cId=3175393 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120718160812/http://www.1up.com/do/feature?cId=3175393 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 18, 2012 |title=Top 5 Enemies I Feel Sorry For from |work=[[1Up.com]] |first=Scott |last=Sharkey|access-date=August 10, 2010}}</ref>

GLaDOS has received praise for her humor and wit. In his review of ''Portal'', ''[[PC Gamer]]'' editor Tom Francis stated that he could hardly stop himself from laughing at GLaDOS's deranged writing.<ref name="3DEgi">{{cite web |title=PC Review: Portal |url=http://www.computerandvideogames.com/article.php?id=172999&site=pcg |publisher=[[Computer and Video Games]] |access-date=August 24, 2009 |date=October 10, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080625193828/http://www.computerandvideogames.com/article.php?id=172999&site=pcg |archive-date=June 25, 2008}}</ref> [[PC Zone]] UK listed her as the second-best conceived character in gaming, commenting that the memes related to the Weighted Companion Cube and "[[The cake is a lie]]" could distract people from GLaDOS's perfected and entertaining voice actress. He described GLaDOS as the "humorous, clinical, savage and poignant heart of ''Portal''".<ref name="pczoneuk">{{cite web |url=http://www.gamesradar.com/f/getting-into-characters/a-2008052810263157029/p-4 |title=Getting into characters... |work=GamesRadar |date=May 28, 2008 |access-date=August 10, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191017045807/https://www.gamesradar.com/getting-into-characters/ |archive-date=October 17, 2019 |url-status=live}}</ref> In a piece in [[The Observer]], game theorist and author of [[Fun Inc]] Tom Chatfield listed GLaDOS as one of the ten best video game characters of all time, describing her both as "gaming's funniest, freakiest female" and a "psychopathic artificial intelligence".<ref name="U8gZI">{{cite news |last=Chatfield |first=Tom |url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2010/aug/08/10-best-video-game-characters |title=The 10 best video-game characters |work=[[The Guardian]] |date=August 8, 2010 |access-date=August 10, 2010 |location=London |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130927110317/http://www.theguardian.com/technology/2010/aug/08/10-best-video-game-characters |archive-date=September 27, 2013 |url-status=live}}</ref> ''The Observer''{{'}}s Will Freeman wrote that GLaDOS "really is (in a rare case of living up to the hyperbole) one of the most fascinating characters in the history of the video game".<ref name="zcwGt">{{cite news |last=Freeman |first=Will |url=https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2011/apr/24/portal-2-will-freeman-review |title=Portal 2 – review|work=[[The Guardian]] |date=April 24, 2011 |access-date=May 4, 2011 |location=London |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140106094156/http://www.theguardian.com/technology/2011/apr/24/portal-2-will-freeman-review |archive-date=January 6, 2014 |url-status=live}}</ref>

The [[Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences]] praised ''Portal'' for its comedy, citing GLaDOS's humorous and homicidal personality.<ref name="mQkjP">{{cite web |url=http://www.interactive.org/events/event_details.asp?idEvents=1 |title=April Game Deconstruction Group Examines Call of Duty 4 and Portal |work=[[Academy of Interactive Arts & Sciences]] |access-date=August 18, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081206101809/http://www.interactive.org/events/event_details.asp?idEvents=1 |archive-date=December 6, 2008}}</ref> Writer Lou Kesten, in discussing humor in video games, cited GLaDOS as possibly being the first time he discovered that video games could make him laugh out loud.<ref name="ynEi5">{{cite news |url=https://www.foxnews.com/story/review-comedic-video-games-bring-the-funny |title=Review: Comedic Video Games Bring the Funny |work=[[Fox News]]|date=May 29, 2008 |access-date=August 18, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110203004823/http://www.foxnews.com/story/0,2933,360263,00.html |archive-date=February 3, 2011 |url-status=live}}</ref> ''[[The New York Times]]'' editor Charles Herold praised GLaDOS, calling her comments "wildly funny".<ref name="JLxic">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/10/25/technology/circuits/25game.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |title=In 1 Box, 3 New Games Filled With Puzzles and Fights |first=Charles |last=Herold |date=October 25, 2007 |access-date=February 21, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161202062007/http://www.nytimes.com/2007/10/25/technology/circuits/25game.html |archive-date=December 2, 2016 |url-status=live}}</ref> In an article titled "The GLaDOS Effect – Can Antagonists Rule the World?", [[Gamasutra]] publisher Simon Carless describes her as the one true memorable character from ''Portal''.
