=== Comparison to other characters in fiction ===
[[File:Hal 9000 Panel.svg|thumb|upright|GLaDOS drew many comparisons to [[HAL 9000]] from the film ''2001: A Space Odyssey''.]]
GLaDOS has been compared to other AI characters in fiction, including [[HAL 9000]] from the film ''2001: A Space Odyssey'' by [[LucasArts]] designer [[Noah Falstein]]. Falstein described her as the best AI he had ever encountered – "more convincingly psychotic than HAL, with a more emotionally engaging death than [[Planetfall|Floyd]], and funnier than [[C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2]]."<ref name="falstein">{{cite web |url=http://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/3616/design_language_the_portal_.php?print=1 |title=Features - Design Language: The Portal Paradoxes |first=Noah |last=Falstein|work=[[Gamasutra]]|access-date=August 10, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100510175329/http://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/3616/design_language_the_portal_.php?print=1 |archive-date=May 10, 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

The comparison was also made by other critics such as journalist Stephen Totilo and IGN's Cindy White. Totilo wrote that HAL was an influence on GLaDOS's psychotic breakdown seen near the end of the first ''Portal'' title. White wrote HAL and GLaDOS were similar due to both having a calm and innocent demeanor that hides their true intentions; she also added that "the prospect of being shut down causes them to act out in deadly ways".<ref name="halglados">{{cite web |last=White |first=Cindy |url=https://www.ign.com/articles/2011/04/20/five-movies-to-watch-if-you-like-portal-2 |title=Movies to Watch if You Like Portal 2 |publisher=IGN |date=April 20, 2011 |access-date=October 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110430034522/http://bluray.ign.com/articles/116/1163020p1.html |archive-date=April 30, 2011 |url-status=live}}</ref>  GamesRadar editor Tyler Wilde stated that while the staff of GamesRadar loves GLaDOS, it makes no sense to insert a personality core into a robot. He suggested that the scientists either never read ''2001: A Space Odyssey'', or read it too much.<ref name="31kIC">{{cite web |url=http://www.gamesradar.com/f/robots-that-dont-make-any-sense/a-201007159042739091/p-2 |title=Robots that don't make any sense |publisher=GamesRadar |date=July 15, 2010 |access-date=August 10, 2010 |archive-date=March 11, 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240311154634/https://www.gamesradar.com/robots-that-dont-make-any-sense/ |url-status=live }}</ref> Empire Online listed her as the 12th-best video game character of all time, describing her acts as "HAL-like conduct".<ref name="tFMyV">{{cite web |url=http://www.empireonline.com/features/50-greatest-video-game-characters/default.asp?film=12 |title=The 50 Greatest Video Game Characters | 12. GLaDOS |work=[[Empire (magazine)|Empire]] |access-date=August 10, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20111226092800/http://www.empireonline.com/features/50-greatest-video-game-characters/default.asp?film=12 |archive-date=December 26, 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Writer Stephen Totilo alluded the final battle with GLaDOS to the scene of David from ''2001'' disabling HAL, with both scenes involving de-evolving the respective characters.<ref name="totilo">{{cite web |url=http://www.mtv.com/news/2456162/the-complete-portal-vs-mode-full-croal-and-totilo-exchange/ |title=The Complete 'Portal' Vs. Mode - Full Croal And Totilo Exchange |publisher=MTV |date=November 21, 2007 |access-date=October 28, 2021 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130208123019/http://multiplayerblog.mtv.com/2007/11/21/the-complete-%E2%80%98portal%E2%80%99-vs-mode-full-croal-and-totilo-exchange/%23more-1660 |archive-date=February 8, 2013 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

[[MSNBC]] game reviewer Blake Snow compared The Sign Painter from ''[[World of Goo]]'' to GLaDOS, due to the mischievousness and unseen nature of the character.<ref name="uzoSO">{{cite web |title=Quit your job and make your game |url=http://www.nbcnews.com/id/27811798/wid/23887017#.WqH4-iznbIU |publisher=[[MSNBC]] |access-date=March 9, 2018 |date=November 25, 2008 |first=Winda |last=Benedetti |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180224173302/http://www.nbcnews.com/id/27811798/wid/23887017#.WqH4-iznbIU |archive-date=February 24, 2018 |url-status=dead}}</ref> GamesRadar editor Mikel Reparaz compared GLaDOS to [[SHODAN]] from the ''[[System Shock]]'' series and stated that before GLaDOS broke their hearts, they had SHODAN.<ref name="b1p9p">{{cite web |last=Reparaz |first=Mikel |title=The scariest villains EVER |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/the-scariest-villains-ever/ |publisher=[[GamesRadar]] |access-date=March 9, 2018 |date=June 13, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180225205451/https://www.gamesradar.com/the-scariest-villains-ever/ |archive-date=February 25, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> GamesRadar's Alan Bradley named GLaDOS as one of gaming's most malicious machines, and a "sort of [[spiritual successor]]" to SHODAN.<ref name="XDWwA">{{cite web |url=https://www.gamesradar.com/gamings-most-malicious-machines/ |last=Bradley |first=Alan |title=Gaming's most malicious machines |publisher=GamesRadar |date=April 8, 2011 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180309120429/https://www.gamesradar.com/gamings-most-malicious-machines/ |archive-date=March 9, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> However, PC Zone UK commented that the comparisons between GLaDOS and SHODAN run dry; while ''Portal'' leaves everything to the players' imagination, ''System Shock 2'' has a strongly defined storyline. They do, however, describe her breakdown as hysterical, desperate, and hilariously childish, calling it the most finely controlled breakdown since [[Patrick Bateman]]'s in the book ''[[American Psycho]]''.<ref name="pczoneuk" /> ''The Daily Telegraph'' editors Nick Cowen and Tom Hoggins listed her as the ninth-greatest video game villain, stating that she is as diabolical as a female AI can get, mentioning SHODAN as being inferior in this respect.<ref name="8Zlj3">{{cite news |last=Cowen |first=Nick |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/technology/video-games/6140189/Top-10-video-game-villains.html |title=Top 10 video game villains |work=Telegraph |date=September 10, 2009 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |location=London |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180224113224/http://www.telegraph.co.uk/technology/video-games/6140189/Top-10-video-game-villains.html |archive-date=February 24, 2018 |url-status=live}}</ref> Writer [[N'Gai Croal]] commented that the boss battle with GLaDOS is similar to the "Room 19" encounter with [[Andrew Ryan (BioShock)|Andrew Ryan]] from ''BioShock'', citing the same use of tactical language and techniques between the two.<ref name="totilo" /> In the book ''Extra Lives: Why Video Games Matter'', [[Infinity Ward]] developer Michael Boon mentioned GLaDOS and BioShock character Andrew Ryan while discussing believable non-playable characters. He commented that while shooting games in general feature enemies as bullet magnets, both Andrew Ryan and GLaDOS do not provide an opportunity for players to shoot them. However, he adds that both characters end up defeating themselves, but in different ways. He stated that she was entertaining, but also that he wanted to kill her. The book's author [[Tom Bissell]] stated that in addition to these similarities, both were well written, describing them as "funny, strange, cruel, and alive."<ref name="wERwL">{{cite book |last=Bissell |first=Tom |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=p3pCgbJp_F0C |title=Extra Lives: Why Video Games Matter |publisher=Random House Digital, Inc. |page=80 |year=2010 |isbn=9780307379283 |access-date=October 15, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170119145214/https://books.google.com/books?id=p3pCgbJp_F0C |archive-date=January 19, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref>

===Character analysis===
In his analysis of ''Portal'', Daniel Johnson pointed out that a majority of ''Portal''{{'}}s plot derived from GLaDOS's dialogue, which he says tells "a metaphoric tale of a power struggle of identity roles within an institution". He discussed how the backstage of the institution is hinted at and gradually revealed through GLaDOS's slip-ups, from the momentary glitch during her initial instructions to the player ("the first flaw in the routine") to her ultimate abandonment of the formal language of the institution as she desperately pleads with the player to return to the testing area (the "front stage", where the institution's inner workings are supposedly hidden from view).<ref name="nhHe8">{{cite news |url=https://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/23960/Analysis_Portal_and_the_Deconstruction_of_the_Institution.php |title=News - Analysis: Portal and the Deconstruction of the Institution |last=Johnson |first=Daniel |work=[[Gamasutra]] |date=June 11, 2009 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107060157/https://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/23960/Analysis_Portal_and_the_Deconstruction_of_the_Institution.php |archive-date=November 7, 2017 |url-status=dead}}</ref> [[Xbox Game Studios|Microsoft Game Studios]] developer Tom Abernathy, in discussing the importance of compelling characters in video games, praises ''Portal'' for inviting the audience to read between the lines to understand GLaDOS's motivations, which gives room for subjective interpretation. His own interpretation is that GLaDOS is conflicted between her wants and needs, a conflict which causes her to go crazy.<ref name="vrOF9">{{cite news |url=https://www.gamasutra.com/php-bin/news_index.php?story=20252 |title=News - AGDC: MGS' Abernathy Talks Importance Of Game Characters |last=Nutt |first=Christian |work=[[Gamasutra]] |date=September 16, 2008 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180225064743/https://www.gamasutra.com/php-bin/news_index.php?story=20252 |archive-date=February 25, 2018 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Stephen Totilo notes the artful way in which GLaDOS's antagonistic character is slowly revealed and defined throughout ''Portal'' despite the minimal interactivity in its storytelling. Of his own reaction to that character development, he writes, "I wanted to hunt GLaDOS down, confront her for her lies, and break free of her clutches. I wanted this boss battle. I don't know if I ever have wanted a boss battle before." ''[[Newsweek]]'' editor N'Gai Croal describes her as a "maternal, mischievous, malevolent and finally murderous unreliable narrator".<ref name="totilo" />

Video game developer Nathan Frost describes ''Portal'' as an exploration of someone with [[narcissistic personality disorder]]. He adds that in order to fulfill her self-centered narcissistic desire to toy with someone, the player-character is trapped in the Enrichment Center, forced to do tricks for the computer. However, once the player-character becomes skilled enough to break the confines of the center, GLaDOS's secure amusement gives way to "histrionic, bipolar deportment". He describes this as a parallel to how a real-life narcissist might attempt to secure the admiration of another person by empowering them in some ways, but limiting them in others. He adds that this works out well for the narcissist until the other person learns to think and act for themselves. He concludes by saying that a part of ''Portal''{{'}}s resonance comes from the fact that using the portal gun to escape the center is a distinct metaphor for escaping an intimate relationship with someone who has narcissism.<ref name="valve creative process" /> [[Grant Tavinor]], author of ''The Art of Videogames'', wrote that GLaDOS's actions and personality in ''Portal'' were \the best of science fiction tropes, and describes her as "insincere, malfunctioning, and probably insane".<ref name="rCg0e">{{cite book |last=Tavinor |first=Grant |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=LM3hnwGb8xUC |title=The art of videogames |publisher=John Wiley and Sons |year=2009 |isbn=9781444310184 |access-date=October 15, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170119144224/https://books.google.com/books?id=LM3hnwGb8xUC |archive-date=January 19, 2017 |url-status=live}}</ref> Wendy Despain, author of ''Writing for Video Games Genres: from FPS to RPG'', used ''Portal'' as an example of a modern classic video game and how modern games tell their stories. She called GLaDOS an "endlessly cheerful and clearly insane computer" and called her narrative "simple".<ref name="nSfC9">{{cite book |last=Despain |first=Wendy |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IodvUgBggnUC |title=Writing for video game genres: from FPS to RPG |publisher=A K Peters, Ltd. |year=2009 |isbn=9781568814179 |access-date=October 15, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140104152025/http://books.google.com/books?id=IodvUgBggnUC |archive-date=January 4, 2014 |url-status=live}}</ref> [[Emily Short]], creator of a female artificial intelligence character in the video game ''[[Galatea (video game)|Galatea]]'', speculates that GLaDOS's final remarks to Chell ("No one likes you, you know") hint that she's talking about herself, not Chell. That she desires an emotional connection, but can't due to her need to see humanity as a threat. "[She has] learned that the humans view her as potentially threatening and essentially disposable, and so she has to see them the same way."<ref name="noTFZ">{{cite web |last=Short |first=Emily |url=http://emshort.wordpress.com/2008/03/24/still-alive/ |title=Still Alive |date=March 24, 2008 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160129021623/https://emshort.wordpress.com/2008/03/24/still-alive/ |archive-date=January 29, 2016 |url-status=live}}</ref>

Scott Rogers, author of the book ''Level Up!: The Guide to Great Video Game Design'', uses GLaDOS as an example of a "tormentor" boss character, stating that she taunts and challenges the players, but does not directly confront or attack them.<ref name="KIIiR">{{Cite book |last=Rogers |first=Scott |title=Level Up!: The Guide to Great Video Game Design |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=8w_ETFmHrewC |publisher=John Wiley and Sons |year=2010 |page=318 |isbn=9780470970928 |access-date=October 15, 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161213155242/https://books.google.com/books?id=8w_ETFmHrewC |archive-date=December 13, 2016 |url-status=live}}</ref> Video game developer Andrew Doull describes the "[[unreliable narrator]]" as a narrative staple from more traditional media, but that GLaDOS is the best example of this staple in gaming. He cites a scene in ''Portal'' where GLaDOS tells the player-character that the current puzzle is unsolvable, which turns out to be false. However, he comments that "it is still incredible to see the number of people who fail to read the situation, and proceed calmly to their death" in the incinerator when ordered to do so by GLaDOS; he uses this example to support an argument that the "unreliable narrator" narrative technique might not transfer readily to the gaming medium.<ref name="Tm8UC">{{cite web |last=Doull |first=Andrew |url=http://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/24753/ |title=Analysis: Narrative - A Montage Without Music |work=[[Gamasutra]] |date=August 14, 2009 |access-date=August 10, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020055856/http://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/24753/ |archive-date=October 20, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Relationship to other characters ===
Associate Professor of English at the [[University of Wisconsin–Stevens Point]] G. Christopher Williams discussed the relationship between GLaDOS and Chell in response to a quote by designer Erik Wolpaw which read "We wanted you to have this very intimate connection with this AI that changes and evolves over time, leading up to the point that you betray her and do the most intimate act you can do with someone—murdering them in cold blood." Williams noted that while this definition of intimacy first seems confusing, the idea of an evolving relationship with an authority figure that eventually leads to betrayal by violating their rules "is an altogether familiar one." He used the parent-child relationship as an example of this and cited a metaphor by psychologist [[Sigmund Freud]] about the murder of a parent, which was meant to describe how children eventually would attempt to get out from under the wing of their parents. Williams wrote "nothing can be as intimate, perhaps, as loving someone enough to follow their rules and then needing to "kill them" in order to escape that "game," which makes this game feel like a really familiar relationship". He pointed her out as one of many examples of authorities that teach the player the controls, the rules, then pushed them towards the goal of their own desire; he stated that "this is an experience that I have every time that I fire up my Xbox and describes the curiously intimate relationship between player and gaming system that emerges in single player gameplay". He further discussed that he had no idea what Chell's name was or that she was a female because he saw the character as himself. He added that he cared about GLaDOS only because he felt that she was commanding him, personally, followed by her wanting to ''kill him'', personally.<ref name="Fzkzz">{{cite web |author=G. Christopher Williams |url=http://www.popmatters.com/pm/post/123220-an-intimate-moment-with-the-computer/ |title=An Intimate Moment With the Computer: PopMatters |work=[[PopMatters]] |date=March 30, 2010 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121125203417/http://www.popmatters.com/pm/post/123220-an-intimate-moment-with-the-computer/ |archive-date=November 25, 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref>

G. Christopher Williams also discussed the relationship between Wheatley and GLaDOS. His initial impression was that Wheatley, being an "utter moron" and attached to GLaDOS, was a political critique of the [[Presidency of George W. Bush]], namely the discussion surrounding the origins of how he gained the office; however, as he progressed, he saw nothing more to suggest that this was the intent. Although he said that the thought of this concept helped make him realize how ''Portal 2'' presents a fundamental issue involving the dynamic between competency and power. In contrast to this, he wrote that the first Portal abundantly displayed that a leader of high intelligence can be the most oppressive force in an organization, and that GLaDOS's "leadership" perfectly parallels sadistic fascism. He also discussed the lack of choice for Chell, who is required to reinstate GLaDOS into her position to escape. He wrote that this lack of choice "manages to effectively maintain its position on the relationship between the everyman and systems of power".<ref name="u1Lra">{{cite web |author=G. Christopher Williams |url=http://www.popmatters.com/pm/post/140262-portal-2-and-the-politics-of-stupidity/ |title='Portal 2' and the Politics of Stupidity: PopMatters |work=[[PopMatters]] |date=April 26, 2011 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121125223156/http://www.popmatters.com/pm/post/140262-portal-2-and-the-politics-of-stupidity/ |archive-date=November 25, 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref>

{{Quote box
| width = 25%
| quote = "By fulfilling the expected obligations of a 1950s 'wife', Caroline sounds as if she might as well be married to Johnson, and after all, given Johnson's alignment with American exceptionalism and what it can achieve through technology, he is the 'science' that she has married herself to."
| source = —Quote from Associate Professor of English at [[University of Wisconsin-Stevens Point]], G. Christopher Williams.<ref name="caroline" />
}}
Williams also discussed the relationship between Caroline, the form she held before she became GLaDOS, and Cave Johnson. He wrote that the relationship of Caroline and Johnson paralleled the saying that "behind every good man is a good woman", due to his dependency on Caroline in order to execute his plans as well as to provide support for the man, himself. He also added that while Cave Johnson jokingly tells his listeners that 'pretty as a postcard' Caroline is off limits because 'She's married. To Science,' he's essentially preventing possible competition. "He is the "science" that she has married herself to".<ref name="caroline">{{cite web |author=G. Christopher Williams |url=http://www.popmatters.com/pm/post/140585-her-name-is-caroline-naming-the-misbehaving-woman-in-portal-2/ |title="Her Name Is Caroline": Identifying the Misbehaving Woman in 'Portal 2': PopMatters |work=[[PopMatters]] |date=May 3, 2011 |access-date=March 9, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121120120310/http://www.popmatters.com/pm/post/140585-her-name-is-caroline-naming-the-misbehaving-woman-in-portal-2/ |archive-date=November 20, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

===As a woman in video games===
Professor G. Christopher Williams wrote that the addition of an "intelligence dampening sphere" performed by scientists on GLaDOS before the events of ''Portal'' could represent men's response to thoughts from women that they see as "misbehavior." He also wrote "the effort to 'dampen' intelligence becomes a rather literal manifestation of the labeling of women as 'dumb' or 'irrational' and the need to control such 'poor' behavior"; he then cited how Wheatley was given a masculine voice and that it could represent a man's intention to remind her of her "stupidity" and to behave better.<ref name="caroline" />

''GamePro''{{'}}s Chris Holt discussed GLaDOS as an icon of feminism, and wrote that as opposed to being an "archetypal villain", she is a "prototypical bound woman". He added that "A female protagonist murdering a female villainess (or vice versa) is not what is interesting to us as critics, but it's the idea that despite her seemingly robotic, unemotional and unstoppable nature, GLaDOS appears vulnerable, sympathetic, and even a victim herself". He inferred that GLaDOS becomes intensified because of the danger she shows to a misogynistic society, and that by destroying the personality cores, "Chell is stripping her of the layers that society has deemed necessary for her to wear" which makes her all the more dangerous. He added that Chell and GLaDOS serve as opposing sides of femininity; where Chell is devoted and fulfills any task given, GLaDOS is aggressive and arguably hazardous to the traditions of a male-dominated world. He also described Chell as a "domestic icon" while he described GLaDOS as a "progressive, intelligent working woman" and that by killing her, Chell can be seen as the obedient, "safe" woman overtaking the "dangerous" rebel feminist. He also cited the use of poems by [[Emily Dickinson]], whom he compares to GLaDOS in how both were reclusive and were essentially disembodied voices.<ref name="Ejqkp">{{cite web |last=Holt |first=Chris |url=http://www.gamepro.com/article/features/218965/portal-s-glados-as-feminist-icon-cont/ |title=Portal's GLaDOS as Feminist Icon, page 2, Feature Story from |publisher=GamePro |access-date=May 5, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110818142135/http://www.gamepro.com/article/features/218965/portal-s-glados-as-feminist-icon-cont/ |archive-date=August 18, 2011 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

''[[IGN]]'' wrote that she diverted all of the stereotypes of a woman in video games and "became one of the most memorable and well-loved characters ever conceived".<ref name="0H3bb">{{cite web |last=Kolan |first=Nick |url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2011/01/08/bringing-a-bikini-to-a-sword-fight?page=2 |title=Bringing a Bikini to a Sword Fight |publisher=IGN |date=February 16, 2011 |access-date=May 5, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121109045542/http://www.ign.com/articles/2011/01/08/bringing-a-bikini-to-a-sword-fight?page=2 |archive-date=November 9, 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref> GamesRadar's Joe McNeilly wrote that ''Portal'' felt like a feminist critique of the FPS genre, which he found to be perfectly executed in the game. He called her a "maternal female construct" and that while she was programmed to react empathetically to the player, she is incapable of feeling emotion. As a result, he felt that she "comes to represent man's attempt to construct an idealized mother figure through the cold logic of science".<ref name="Rhh4e">{{cite web |url=http://www.gamesradar.com/xbox360/f/portal-is-the-most-subversive-game-ever/a-20071207115329881080/g-2006071916221774024 |title=Portal is the most subversive game ever, Portal Xbox 360 Features |first=Joe|last=McNeilly|publisher=GamesRadar |date=December 7, 2007 |access-date=May 5, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080516005851/http://www.gamesradar.com/xbox360/f/portal-is-the-most-subversive-game-ever/a-20071207115329881080/g-2006071916221774024 |archive-date=May 16, 2008 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Although Stephanie Harkin described GLaDOS instead as an emotionally abusive mother figure.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Harkin |first1=Stephanie |date=December 19, 2018 |title="The Only Thing You've Managed to Break So Far Is My Heart": An Analysis of Portal's Monstrous Mother GLaDOS |url=https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1555412018819663 |journal=Games and Culture |volume=15 |issue=5 |pages=529–543 |doi=10.1177/1555412018819663 |s2cid=149637584 |access-date=February 17, 2023 |archive-date=February 17, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230217233133/https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/10.1177/1555412018819663 |url-status=live |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

In discussing the lack of female heroes in video games, particularly in video games published by [[Activision]], Gamasutra news director Leigh Alexander cited GLaDOS while arguing that the "females do not sell" notion is possibly false logic, stating that she was on the fast track to becoming one of gaming's most beloved characters.<ref name="69tpR">{{cite web |last=Alexander |first=Leigh |url=http://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/29719/InDepth_No_Female_Heroes_At_Activision.php |title=In-Depth: No Female Heroes At Activision? |work=[[Gamasutra]] |date=August 4, 2010 |access-date=August 10, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100806064936/http://www.gamasutra.com/view/news/29719/InDepth_No_Female_Heroes_At_Activision.php |archive-date=August 6, 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Gamasutra writers Leigh Alexander, [[Brandon Boyer]], Simon Carless, and Christian Nutt listed GLaDOS as being the second-most affecting video game character, being the highest-ranked actual character because the most affecting video game character was the player. They attribute the overall quality of ''Portal'' to GLaDOS, stating that without her, ''Portal'' would not be nearly as quotable. They added that the relationship between GLaDOS and the player-character has been described as passive-aggressive, maternal, and a "feminist manifesto".<ref name="affecting">{{cite web |title=Top 5 Most Affecting Characters |url=http://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/3228/gamasutras_best_of_2007.php?page=2 |work=[[Gamasutra]]|access-date=August 25, 2009 |date=December 31, 2007 |first1=Leigh|last1= Alexander|first2= Brandon|last2= Boyer|first3= Simon |last3=Carless|first4=Christian|last4= Nutt|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091109222044/http://www.gamasutra.com/view/feature/3228/gamasutras_best_of_2007.php?page=2 |archive-date=November 9, 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

GrandPat Star (grandfather) }} '''Patrick Star''' is a fictional character in [[Nickelodeon]]'s [[animated television series]] ''[[SpongeBob SquarePants]]''. He is voiced by actor [[Bill Fagerbakke]] and was created and designed by [[marine biology|marine biologist]] and animator [[Stephen Hillenburg]]. He first appeared in the series' pilot episode "[[Help Wanted (SpongeBob SquarePants)|Help Wanted]]" on May 1, 1999. In addition to his supporting role on ''SpongeBob SquarePants'', Patrick also serves as the main protagonist of ''[[The Patrick Star Show]]'', which premiered in 2021.{{Cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie |date=August 10, 2020 |title=''SpongeBob SquarePants'' Spinoff Series ''The Patrick Star Show'' Set At Nickelodeon |url=https://deadline.com/2020/08/spongebob-squarepants-spinoff-series-the-patrick-star-show-set-nickelodeon-bill-fagerbakke-1203006633/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200811013253/https://deadline.com/2020/08/spongebob-squarepants-spinoff-series-the-patrick-star-show-set-nickelodeon-bill-fagerbakke-1203006633/ |archive-date=August 11, 2020 |access-date=August 10, 2020 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]]}} An [[overweight]] [[Anthropomorphism|anthropomorphic]] coral pink [[starfish]], Patrick lives under a rock in the underwater city of Bikini Bottom, and is the best friend of [[SpongeBob SquarePants (character)|SpongeBob SquarePants]]. His most significant character traits are his laziness and [[stupidity|low intelligence]], although he occasionally shows surprising intelligence. Patrick is unemployed and a self-proclaimed expert in the "art of doing nothing". The character has received positive reactions from critics and fans alike. Patrick has been included in various ''SpongeBob SquarePants''-related merchandise, including trading cards, video games, plush toys, and comic books. He is also a leading character in the [[SpongeBob SquarePants (film series)|four films]] and [[SpongeBob SquarePants (musical)|stage musical]] based on the franchise. ==Development== ===Creation and design=== [[Stephen Hillenburg]] first became fascinated with the ocean and began developing his artistic abilities as a child. During college, he majored in [[marine biology]] and minored in art. He planned to return to college eventually to pursue a [[master's degree]] in art. After graduating in 1984, he joined the [[Ocean Institute]], an organization dedicated to educating the public about [[oceanography|marine science]] and [[maritime history]].{{cite web|url=http://www.ocean-institute.org/|title=Welcome to the Ocean Institute|work=ocean-institute.org|access-date=December 24, 2013|archive-date=November 16, 2013|archive-url=https://archive.today/20131116022048/http://www.ocean-institute.org/|url-status=live}}{{cite video |people=[[Thomas F. Wilson|Wilson, Thomas F.]](Interviewer); Hillenburg, Stephen (Interviewee) |date=May 29, 2012 |title=Big Pop Fun #28: Stephen Hillenburg, Artist and Animator–Interview |url=http://ec.libsyn.com/p/d/9/8/d98c6fd6cc81f188/BPF28_Stephen_Hillenburg_artist_and_animator.mp3?d13a76d516d9dec20c3d276ce028ed5089ab1ce3dae902ea1d01c08031d1c85f7cb2&c_id=4560686 |format=mp3 |medium=Podcast |publisher=[[Nerdist Industries]] |access-date=December 21, 2013 |archive-url=https://www.webcitation.org/6M1QBJ1BZ?url=http://ec.libsyn.com/p/d/9/8/d98c6fd6cc81f188/BPF28_Stephen_Hillenburg_artist_and_animator.mp3?d13a76d516d9dec20c3d276ce028ed5089ab1ce3dae902ea1d01c08031d1c85f7cb2&c_id=4560686 |archive-date=2013-12-21}} While he was there, he initially had the idea that would lead to the creation of ''SpongeBob SquarePants'': a comic book titled ''The Intertidal Zone''. In 1987, Hillenburg left the institute to pursue a career in animation.{{cite video | people=Hillenburg, Stephen|date=2003|title=The Origin of SpongeBob SquarePants. SpongeBob SquarePants: The Complete First Season| medium=DVD|publisher=Paramount Home Entertainment}}{{Cite book|last=Banks|first=Steven|others= Gregg Schigiel (Illustrator)|title=SpongeBob Exposed! The Insider's Guide to SpongeBob SquarePants|publisher=Simon Spotlight/Nickelodeon|location=[[New York City]], [[New York (state)|New York]]|date=September 24, 2004|isbn=978-0-689-86870-2|page=9}} A few years after studying experimental animation at the [[California Institute of the Arts]], Hillenburg met [[Joe Murray (animator)|Joe Murray]], creator of the Nickelodeon series ''[[Rocko's Modern Life]]'', at an animation festival, and was offered a job as a director of the show.{{cite video | people=[[Joe Murray (animator)|Murray, Joe]]|date=2003|title=The Origin of SpongeBob SquarePants. SpongeBob SquarePants: The Complete First Season| medium=DVD|publisher=Paramount Home Entertainment}}{{Cite book|title=Makin' Toons: Inside the Most Popular Animated TV Shows and Movies|publisher=Allworth Communications, Inc|last=Neuwirth|first=Allan|isbn=978-1-58115-269-2|year=2003|page=[https://archive.org/details/makintoonsinside0000neuw/page/50 50]|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/makintoonsinside0000neuw/page/50}}"[http://www.title14.com/rocko/contributors/murray.html Lisa (Kiczuk) Trainor interviews Joe Murray, creator of Rocko's Modern Life] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20150420193919/http://www.title14.com/rocko/contributors/murray.html |date=April 20, 2015 }}," ''The Rocko's Modern Life FAQ'' [[Martin Olson]], one of the writers for ''Rocko's Modern Life'', read ''The Intertidal Zone'' and encouraged Hillenburg to create a television series with a similar concept. At that point, Hillenburg had not even considered creating his own series. However, he realized that if he ever did, this would be the best approach.{{cite AV media|last1=Hillenburg|first1=Stephen|last2=Murray|first2=Joe|last3=Drymon|first3=Derek|last4=Coleman|first4=Eric|last5=Hecht|first5=Albie|date=2003|title=The Origin of SpongeBob SquarePants. [[File:Patrick Star by Stephen Hillenburg (bible).jpg|thumb|left|270px|Early drawings of Patrick from [[Stephen Hillenburg]]'s [[bible (screenwriting)|bible]]]] For the show's characters, Hillenburg started to draw and used character designs from his comic book—including starfish, [[crab]], and [[sponge]]. He described Patrick as "probably the dumbest guy in town".Hillenburg, Stephen. (March 1, 2003). ''The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie'' (''The Absorbing Tale Behind The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie'') (DVD). Paramount Home Entertainment/Nickelodeon. The character was conceived as a starfish to embody the animal's nature; according to Hillenburg, starfish look "dumb and slow", but they are "very active and aggressive" in reality, like Patrick.Hillenburg, Stephen. (March 1, 2003). ''The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie'' (''The Case of the Sponge "Bob"'') (DVD). Paramount Home Entertainment/Nickelodeon. Hillenburg incorporated [[character comedy]] rather than [[topical humor]] on the show to emphasize "things that are more about humorous situations and about characters and their flaws."{{Cite web |last=Burnet |first=Jaime |date=November 18, 2004 |title=Movie Interview: The unbearable lightness of SpongeBob |url=http://www.thegauntlet.ca/story/movie-interview-unbearable-lightness-spongebob |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140427032528/http://www.thegauntlet.ca/story/movie-interview-unbearable-lightness-spongebob |archive-date=April 27, 2014 |access-date=April 27, 2014 |website=[[Gauntlet (newspaper)|The Gauntlet]] |publisher=Gauntlet Publication Society}} He designed Patrick and SpongeBob as such because "they're whipping themselves up into situations—that's always where the humor comes from. The rule is: Follow the innocence and avoid topical humor."{{cite news|last=Cavna|first=Michael|title=The Interview: 'SpongeBob' Creator Stephen Hillenburg|url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/comic-riffs/2009/07/_tom_kenny_who_voices.html|newspaper=The Washington Post|access-date=April 27, 2014|date=July 14, 2009|archive-date=October 6, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121006111645/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/comic-riffs/2009/07/_tom_kenny_who_voices.html}} In spite of being depicted as having a good temperament or state of mind, Patrick has been shown in some episodes to have a [[tantrum]]. Patrick's emotional outbreak was originally written only for the [[SpongeBob SquarePants (season 1)|first season]] episode "Valentine's Day", where SpongeBob and [[Sandy Cheeks|Sandy]] try to give Patrick a [[Valentine's Day]] gift, and "was supposed to be a one-time thing". However, according to episode writer [[Jay Lender]], "when that show came back it felt so right that his dark side started popping up everywhere. You can plan ahead all you want, but the characters eventually tell you who they are." Every main character in the show has its own unique footstep sound. The sound of Patrick's footsteps is recorded by the show's [[Foley (filmmaking)|Foley]] crew, with a Foley talent wearing a [[slip-on shoe]]. Jeff Hutchins, show's sound designer said, "[Going] barefoot makes it tough to have much presence, so we decided that Patrick would be performed with shoes on."{{cite news | author = Hutchins, Jeff | title = The Oral History of ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' | work = [[Hogan's Alley (magazine)|Hogan's Alley]] #17 | year = 2010 | access-date = September 21, 2012 | url = http://cartoonician.com/the-oral-history-of-spongebob-squarepants/ | publisher = Bull Moose Publishing Corporation | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150831044034/http://cartoonician.com/the-oral-history-of-spongebob-squarepants/ | archive-date = August 31, 2015 }} ===Voice=== [[File:Bill Fagerbakke on Comic-Con panel (2009) - Cropped.jpg|thumb|200px|[[Bill Fagerbakke]], the voice of Patrick]] Patrick's voice is provided by actor [[Bill Fagerbakke]], who also does the voices of numerous other characters on ''SpongeBob SquarePants''. While creating the show and writing its [[Help Wanted (SpongeBob SquarePants)|pilot episode]] in 1997, Hillenburg and [[Derek Drymon]], the show's then-[[creative director]], were also conducting auditions to find voices for the show's characters.{{cite news | author = Drymon, Derek | title = The Oral History of ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' | work = [[Hogan's Alley (magazine)|Hogan's Alley]] #17 | year = 2010 | access-date = September 21, 2012 | url = http://cartoonician.com/the-oral-history-of-spongebob-squarepants/ | publisher = Bull Moose Publishing Corporation | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150831044034/http://cartoonician.com/the-oral-history-of-spongebob-squarepants/ | archive-date = August 31, 2015 }} Fagerbakke auditioned for the role of Patrick after [[Tom Kenny]], SpongeBob's voice actor, had been cast. Fagerbakke said, "Steve is such a lovely guy, and I had absolutely no feeling for the material whatsoever." He described his experience in the audition, saying "I was just going in for another audition, and I had no idea what was in store there in terms of the remarkable visual wit and really the kind of endearing child-like humanity in the show. I couldn't pick that up from the audition material at all. I was just kind of perfunctorially trying to give the guy what he wanted."{{cite web|last=Liu|first=Ed|title=Being Patrick Star: Toonzone Interviews Bill Fagerbakke on ''SpongeBob SquarePants''|url=http://www.toonzone.net/2013/11/patrick-star-toonzone-interviews-bill-fagerbakke-spongebob-squarepants/|work=Toon Zone|access-date=March 28, 2014|date=November 11, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131219000346/http://www.toonzone.net/2013/11/patrick-star-toonzone-interviews-bill-fagerbakke-spongebob-squarepants/|archive-date=December 19, 2013}} {{blockquote|Steve Hillenburg actually played for me a portion of Tom [Kenny]'s performance as the character, and they were looking for a [[counterpoint]]. And I do the big dumb stuff. That's my deal ... that's what I do {{sic}}. It was such a neat experience. Typically, when you audition for any kind of voiceover stuff, you're in a studio, but as I remember it, this was, like, in a weird conference room somewhere, and he had one of those little old cassette decks that's about half the size of a shoebox, and there was something so endearing about it.|Fagerbakke, on his audition for the role.}} Fagerbakke referred to Patrick as "AquaDauber" (a reference to his role as Michael "Dauber" Dybinski on the 1990s sitcom [[Coach (TV series)|''Coach'']]) in the first few years of working on the show. Patrick is "enormously entertaining to portray" because, according to Fagerbakke, "when I'm performing Patrick, there are many secrets that I could never divulge". Fagerbakke's approach in voicing Patrick is "much the same way I would do [to] any kind of character." "I'm always looking for opportunities to explore that freewheeling imagination and insanity of children. To be able to plug in to that and let that carry you in to a performance is such a gas, I have so much fun with that. I love kids; I raised two girls and I love being a parent", he said. The cast members record as a whole cast. Fagerbakke says that the situation improves his performance as a voice actor because "there is something remarkable that happens when people are working together that is unique to that."{{cite web|last=Burszan|first=David|title=Interview With Bill Fagerbakke: The Voice of SpongeBob's Patrick Star|url=http://www.denofgeek.us/tv/spongebob-squarepants/225197/interview-with-bill-fagerbakke-the-voice-of-spongebobs-patrick-star|publisher=Den of Geek|access-date=April 27, 2014|date=November 11, 2013|archive-date=April 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140427160937/http://www.denofgeek.us/tv/spongebob-squarepants/225197/interview-with-bill-fagerbakke-the-voice-of-spongebobs-patrick-star|url-status=live}} Fagerbakke modeled his performance whenever Patrick is angry after that of American actress [[Shelley Winters]].{{Cite book|last=Banks|first=Steven|others= Gregg Schigiel (Illustrator)|title=SpongeBob Exposed! The Insider's Guide to SpongeBob SquarePants|publisher=Simon Spotlight/Nickelodeon|location=[[New York City]], [[New York (state)|New York]]|date=September 24, 2004|isbn=978-0-689-86870-2|page=33}} Fagerbakke has been compared to Patrick's character, which he concurs with. Kenny said that "Bill [Fagerbakke] is a big guy. The world is almost too small for him. He's a force of nature, like Patrick."{{cite news | author = Kenny, Tom | title = The Oral History of ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' | work = [[Hogan's Alley (magazine)|Hogan's Alley]] #17 | year = 2010 | access-date = September 21, 2012 | url = http://cartoonician.com/the-oral-history-of-spongebob-squarepants/ | publisher = Bull Moose Publishing Corporation | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150831044034/http://cartoonician.com/the-oral-history-of-spongebob-squarepants/ | archive-date = August 31, 2015 }} Writer [[Jay Lender]] said, describing Fagerbakke in the recording studio, "Bill Fagerbakke is the most thoughtful performer I've ever seen in the booth—he was always asking questions and really trying to get into the mindset, such as it is, of Patrick."{{cite news | author = Lender, Jay | title = The Oral History of ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' | work = [[Hogan's Alley (magazine)|Hogan's Alley]] #17 | year = 2010 | access-date = September 21, 2012 | url = http://cartoonician.com/the-oral-history-of-spongebob-squarepants/ | publisher = Bull Moose Publishing Corporation | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150831044034/http://cartoonician.com/the-oral-history-of-spongebob-squarepants/ | archive-date = August 31, 2015 }} Writer [[Kent Osborne]] said of Fagerbakke, "He is this big guy, and he plays Patrick so well. He's just this big guy, and he lumbers around."{{cite news | author = Osborne, Kent | title = The Oral History of ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' | work = [[Hogan's Alley (magazine)|Hogan's Alley]] #17 | year = 2010 | access-date = September 21, 2012 | url = http://cartoonician.com/the-oral-history-of-spongebob-squarepants/ | publisher = Bull Moose Publishing Corporation | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150831044034/http://cartoonician.com/the-oral-history-of-spongebob-squarepants/ | archive-date = August 31, 2015 }} Fagerbakke said, "I'm clumsy. I'm goofy. I make mistakes all the time" and agreed that "I guess I'm a lot of Patrick."Fagerbakke, Bill. (November 16, 2010). Paramount Home Entertainment/Nickelodeon. == Appearances == ===Role in ''SpongeBob SquarePants''=== Patrick is the ignorant but humorous best friend of SpongeBob SquarePants. He is portrayed as being an overweight pink starfish, who serves as the [[village idiot]] of the underwater city of Bikini Bottom.{{cite journal|last=Whipp|first=Glenn|title=An Absorbing Cinema Debut|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-124989759.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140611130219/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-124989759.html|archive-date=June 11, 2014|journal=Daily News|access-date=April 26, 2014|date=November 19, 2004|via=[[HighBeam Research]]|url-access=subscription|url-status=usurped|location=Los Angeles, CA}} Patrick gets dumber throughout the series and has been shown to make many ludicrous mistakes. Despite this, he has occasionally been portrayed as a [[savant syndrome|savant]], with articulate observance to certain subjects in specific detail. However, he always reverts quickly back to his usual, unintelligent self after displaying a moment of wisdom.{{cite episode|title=Squidtastic Voyage|series=SpongeBob SquarePants|season=4|number=75a|airdate=October 6, 2006|credits=Writers: [[Luke Brookshier]], Tom King, Dani Michaeli}} He holds no form of occupation except for several very brief stints working at the [[Krusty Krab]] and at the Chum Bucket in a variety of positions, * {{cite episode|title=Big Pink Loser|series=SpongeBob SquarePants|season=2|number=23a|airdate=November 16, 2000|credits=Writers: Jay Lender, William Reiss, Merriwether Williams}} * {{cite episode|title=The Fry Cook Games|series=SpongeBob SquarePants|season=2|number=39b|airdate=September 28, 2001|credits=Writers: Jay Lender, Dan Povenmire, Merriwether Williams}} * {{cite episode|title=Bummer Vacation|series=SpongeBob SquarePants|season=4|number=74a|airdate=October 13, 2006|credits=Writers: Casey Alexander, Chris Mitchell, Dani Michaeli}} * {{cite episode|title=No Hat for Pat|series=SpongeBob SquarePants|season=6|number=120a|airdate=July 19, 2009|credits=Writers: Casey Alexander, Zeus Cervas, Dani Michaeli}} * {{cite episode|title=Chum Bucket Supreme|series=SpongeBob SquarePants|season=6|number=122a|airdate=July 19, 2009|credits=Writers: Sean Charmatz and Dani Michaeli}} and mostly spends his time either clowning around with SpongeBob, catching jellyfish with him, or lounging beneath the rock under which he resides. According to Kya Buller from ''Tyla'', Patrick's house can be described as a [[visual pun]] on the phrase "[[wikt:live under a rock|living under a rock]]", since Patrick is a dim-witted character who is oblivious to common knowledge.{{cite web|url=https://www.tyla.com/entertainment/tv-and-film/spongebob-patrick-lives-under-rock-reason-518561-20241216|title=SpongeBob fans only just realising why Patrick lives under a rock|author-first1=Kya |author-last1=Buller|date=2024-12-16|website=Tyla}} Moreover, his residence also has a basis in marine biology, since some species of starfish do live under rocks in order to avoid predators and also to wait for their prey.{{cite web|url=https://bubblydiver.com/do-starfish-live-under-rocks/|website=Bubbly Diver|title=Do Starfish Live Under Rocks?}} At home, Patrick is usually depicted either sleeping, watching TV, or engaged in the "art of doing nothing", at which he is an expert.{{cite episode|title=Stanley S. SquarePants|series=SpongeBob SquarePants|season=5|number=100b|airdate=November 23, 2007|credits=Writers: [[Luke Brookshier]], Nate Cash, Eric Shaw}} All the furnishings in the space under his rock are made of sand, and Patrick can simply opt to quickly build up furniture as needed; even so, his living space is sparse and contains only the barest essentials.{{cite episode|title=I'm with Stupid|series=SpongeBob SquarePants|season=2|number=37b|airdate=November 30, 2001|credits=Writers: [[Aaron Springer]], [[C.H. Greenblatt]], [[Mark O'Hare]]}} Aside from his best friend SpongeBob, who is often impressed by Patrick's capacity to come up with naïve yet genius plans or solutions,{{cite episode|title=Texas|series=SpongeBob SquarePants|season=1|number=18a|network=Nickelodeon|airdate=March 22, 2000|credits=Writers: [[Sherm Cohen]], [[Vincent Waller]], David Fain}} Patrick frequently irritates those around him and is confounded by the simplest of questions or subjects.{{cite episode|title=You Don't Know Sponge|series=SpongeBob SquarePants|season=7|number=149a|airdate=August 9, 2010|credits=Writers: [[Luke Brookshier]], Nate Cash, Derek Iversen}} The characters of [[Mr. Krabs]] and Squidward have no patience for Patrick's stupidity, and the former does not pay him much regard; [[Clancy Brown]], who provides Mr. Krabs' voice, said, "The only person that he [Mr. Krabs] doesn't hire is Patrick because Patrick is just too stupid to work for nothing."Brown, Clancy. In the second film, Patrick (along with SpongeBob, Sandy, Squidward, Mr. Krabs, and Plankton) is rendered in 3D (using [[computer-generated imagery|CGI]]) in the live action scenes. The group becomes an "[[Avengers (comics)|''Avengers'']]-type team", better known as "The Spongers"; Patrick transforms to Mr. Superawesomeness.{{cite web|last1=Amidi|first1=Amid |author-link=Amid Amidi|title=First Look: SpongeBob CGI Superhero Feature 'Sponge Out of Water'|url=http://www.cartoonbrew.com/cgi/first-look-cgi-spongebob-superhero-feature-sponge-out-of-water-101963.html|publisher=Cartoon Brew|access-date=May 16, 2015|date=July 24, 2014|archive-date=May 28, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150528062331/http://www.cartoonbrew.com/cgi/first-look-cgi-spongebob-superhero-feature-sponge-out-of-water-101963.html|url-status=live}} In 2009, actor John Fricker portrayed Patrick in the musical adaptation of the third season episode "[[The Sponge Who Could Fly]]".{{cite web|title=Review: SpongeBob SquarePants, Theatre Royal|url=http://www.nottinghampost.com/Review-Spongebob-Squarepants/story-12234729-detail/story.html|work=[[Nottingham Post]]|access-date=April 27, 2014|date=April 30, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140427155734/http://www.nottinghampost.com/Review-Spongebob-Squarepants/story-12234729-detail/story.html|archive-date=April 27, 2014}} Fricker and the musical itself were well received by most critics. Gordon Barr and Roger Domeneghetti of the ''[[Evening Chronicle]]'' described the musical as "a silly riot of colour [...] as you'd have to expect from an adaptation of a cartoon TV show",{{cite news|author1=Barr, Gordon |author2=Domeneghetti, Roger |date=April 23, 2009|title=A Splashing Show|newspaper= [[Evening Chronicle]]|page=29}} while Viv Hardwick of ''[[The Northern Echo]]'' said that Fricker and Martin Johnston ([[Mr. Krabs]]) "win the biggest costume contest."{{cite news|author-last1=Hardwick|author-first1= Viv|title=Theatre critics|date=April 24, 2009|newspaper=[[The Northern Echo]]|page=25}} A critic from the ''[[Chichester Observer]]'' wrote, "John Fricker is in his element as the simple but lovable Patrick Star".{{cite web|title=Review: SpongeBob SquarePants makes a splash at the Mayflower|url=http://www.chichester.co.uk/what-s-on/entertainment/review-spongebob-squarepants-makes-a-splash-at-the-mayflower-1-1511634|work=Chichester Observer|access-date=March 9, 2026|archive-date=April 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140427174302/http://www.chichester.co.uk/what-s-on/entertainment/review-spongebob-squarepants-makes-a-splash-at-the-mayflower-1-1511634|url-status=dead}} The character of Patrick has become viral in the Internet in the forms of [[Internet meme|meme]]s or [[image macro]]s. A still from ''The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie'', which displays Patrick in a drop-jawed look, inspired a [[YouTube]] user to create a presentation of Patrick's expression using a number of different filters. Following this, a YouTube user uploaded another video featuring Patrick reacting to Canadian singer [[Justin Bieber]]'s 2010 single, "[[Baby (Justin Bieber song)|Baby]]". The meme called "Surprised Patrick" started to disseminate, with one of the first images was posted to [[Reddit]] by SeannyOC, and then reblogged onto [[I Can Has Cheezburger?]]'s Memebase.{{cite web|last=May|first=Geoff|title=30 of the Best Surprised Patrick Memes Ever|url=http://www.bite.ca/bitedaily/2013/04/30-of-the-best-surprised-patrick-star-memes-ever/|publisher=[[BiteTV]]|access-date=April 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140427162243/http://www.bite.ca/bitedaily/2013/04/30-of-the-best-surprised-patrick-star-memes-ever/|archive-date=April 27, 2014}} Comedy websites—including [[BiteTV]], [[CollegeHumor]],{{cite web|last=Han|first=Chris|title=Patrick Star is in a State of Permanent Shock Updated|url=http://www.collegehumor.com/post/6880089/patrick-star-is-in-a-state-of-permanent-shock|publisher=[[CollegeHumor]]|access-date=April 27, 2014|date=March 26, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140427164340/http://www.collegehumor.com/post/6880089/patrick-star-is-in-a-state-of-permanent-shock|archive-date=April 27, 2014}} [[Mashable]]{{cite web|last=Prakash|first=Nena|title='Surprised Patrick' Is Shocked by Instant Meme Fame|url=http://mashable.com/2013/03/29/surprised-patrick-meme/|publisher=[[Mashable]]|access-date=April 27, 2014|date=March 30, 2013|archive-date=June 3, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210603084700/https://mashable.com/2013/03/29/surprised-patrick-meme/|url-status=live}} and [[Smosh]]{{cite web|title=Best Of The Surprised Patrick Meme!|url=http://www.smosh.com/smosh-pit/memes/best-surprised-patrick-meme|publisher=[[Smosh]]|access-date=April 27, 2014|year=2013|archive-date=April 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140427154614/http://www.smosh.com/smosh-pit/memes/best-surprised-patrick-meme}}—have published their own "Best of" lists and compilations, covering the "Surprised Patrick" meme's popularity. Mashable's Nena Prakash said, "For years, Patrick Star helped hold down Bikini Bottom while SpongeBob was flippin' burgers at [t]he Krusty Krab. But now it's time for Patrick to come out from under that rock and take a seat upon his royal meme throne, because he's an Internet star(fish)." Another popular meme based on the character is the "Push It Somewhere Else Patrick" image macro, which was taken from the second season episode "Sandy, SpongeBob, and the Worm", based on a scene where Patrick suggests that the town should relocate itself in order to deal with an Alaskan Bull Worm.{{cite web|title=Best Of The 'Push It Somewhere Else Patrick' Meme!|url=http://www.smosh.com/smosh-pit/memes/best-push-it-somewhere-else-patrick-meme|publisher=[[Smosh]]|access-date=April 27, 2014|author=Cosmic Charlie|year=2011|archive-date=April 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140427163653/http://www.smosh.com/smosh-pit/memes/best-push-it-somewhere-else-patrick-meme}} A CGI version of Patrick was part of Nickelodeon's 2022 Christmas Day [[National Football League]] game between the [[Denver Broncos]] and [[Los Angeles Rams]], with Fagerbakke providing real-time commentary for the character. Patrick's most notable call came during a [[Russell Wilson]] interception. ==Reception== ===Critical response=== Critical reception for the character from both professionals and fans has been positive. In his DVD review for ''[[DVD Verdict]]'', Bill Treadway called Patrick "the village idiot, who sometimes gives SpongeBob some really bad advice, but he is a loyal friend and that's something we don't see much of these days." He said, "Patrick is the definition of stupid and his antics will have you laughing out loud."{{cite web|last=Treadway |first=Bill |title=''SpongeBob SquarePants'': The Complete First Season |url=http://www.dvdverdict.com/reviews/spongebobseason1.php |publisher=DVD Verdict |access-date=October 29, 2013 |date=November 10, 2003 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130921131821/http://www.dvdverdict.com/reviews/spongebobseason1.php |archive-date=September 21, 2013 }} In a review published in 2007, Peter Keepnews of ''[[The New York Times]]'' said, "Patrick is a popular character, and the new episodes illustrate why: He is unfailingly enthusiastic, touchingly loyal and absolutely undeterred by his intellectual limitations. Hilariously voiced by Bill Fagerbakke, he is not just an endearing comic creation but a role model for idiots everywhere."{{cite web|last=Keepnews|first=Peter|title=Lincoln? Washington? Nope. Patrick!|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2007/02/19/arts/television/19keep.html?_r=0|access-date=May 1, 2014|work=The New York Times|date=February 19, 2007|archive-date=January 16, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190116201120/https://www.nytimes.com/2007/02/19/arts/television/19keep.html?_r=0|url-status=live}} Nancy Basile of [[About.com]] called Patrick "one of the silliest characters on ''SpongeBob SquarePants''". In her DVD review of "SpongeBob and Friends: Patrick SquarePants", a Patrick-themed ''SpongeBob SquarePants'' home video release, Basile said, "The episodes included [...] are hilarious. They're not only some of Patrick's best episodes, but also some of the show's classic episodes." She ranked "[[SpongeBob SquarePants (season 4)#ep75b|That's No Lady]]" as Patrick's best episode and said, "I was remiss not to include this episode in my top ten [''SpongeBob SquarePants'' episodes] list." She cited her favorite scene from the episode, where "Patrick can't read the number on Mr. Krabs' table, saying, 'Ford knee.' Mr. Krabs replies, 'That's a seven, Patricia.'"{{cite web|last=Basile|first=Nancy|title=SpongeBob and Friends: Patrick SquarePants|url=http://animatedtv.about.com/od/spongebobsquarepants/fl/SpongeBob-and-Friends-Patrick-SquarePants.htm|publisher=[[About.com]]|access-date=April 27, 2014|archive-date=April 27, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020004608/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/kids-choice-awards-2014-winners-692089|url-status=live}} ===Speculated homosexuality=== In 2002, the show's popularity among the [[LGBT community|gay community]] grew, and it was reported that they had embraced the show, according to [[BBC Online]].{{cite web|title=People in the news|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-92666234.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131108172344/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-92666234.html|archive-date=November 8, 2013|work=Knight Ridder|access-date=October 31, 2013|via=HighBeam Research|url-access=subscription|url-status=usurped|date=October 9, 2002}} ''[[The Wall Street Journal]]'' also raised questions about SpongeBob and Patrick in an article that pointed out the show's popularity in the gay community.{{cite web|title=Tom Kenny finds his voice in the world of cartoons|url=http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-119973977.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131108172347/http://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-119973977.html|archive-date=November 8, 2013|work=Chicago Tribune|access-date=October 31, 2013|date=November 25, 2002|via=HighBeam Research|url-access=subscription|url-status=usurped|location=Chicago, IL}} [[Tom Kenny]], in response to the article, said "[I] felt the insinuation was a stretch." "I had heard that gay viewers enjoy the show in the same way that lots of people—college students, parents and children—like the show [...] I thought it was rather silly to hang an entire article on that. I don't think it's a case of it being a gay-friendly show—It's a human-being-friendly show. They're all welcome", Kenny said. In 2005, a promotional video that involves SpongeBob promoting [[cultural diversity|diversity]] and [[Toleration|tolerance]]{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/americas/4190699.stm | title=US right attacks SpongeBob video | date=January 20, 2005 | access-date=June 11, 2007 | author=BBC Staff | publisher=[[BBC News]] | archive-date=March 15, 2009 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090315035331/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/americas/4190699.stm | url-status=live }} was criticized by two U.S. Christian [[Evangelicalism|evangelical]] groups, most notably [[Focus on the Family]], because they saw the character was being used as an advocate for [[homosexuality]] though the video contained "no reference to sex, sexual lifestyle or sexual identity."{{cite news|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/id/wbna6852828|title=Will SpongeBob make you gay?|publisher=[[NBC News]]|access-date=January 21, 2005|archive-date=March 27, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130327024711/http://www.nbcnews.com/id/6852828|url-status=live}}{{cite news | url=https://www.usatoday.com/life/television/2005-01-22-kids-video_x.htm | title=SpongeBob, Muppets and the Sister Sledge writer suffer criticism | date=January 22, 2005 | access-date=June 11, 2007 | agency=Associated Press | work=[[USA Today]] | archive-date=February 4, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120204112303/http://www.usatoday.com/life/television/2005-01-22-kids-video_x.htm | url-status=live }} The incident led to questions as to whether or not SpongeBob, his best friend Patrick, and the rest of the series' characters are homosexual characters. After this speculation and comments, Hillenburg repeated his assertion that sexual preference was never considered during the creation of the show.{{cite web|url=http://www.iol.co.za/index.php?set_id=1&click_id=22&art_id=vn20050129114540161C803463|title=SpongeBob isn't gay or straight, creator says|date=January 29, 2005|publisher=Reuters|access-date=November 9, 2008|archive-date=July 16, 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100716063448/http://www.iol.co.za/index.php?set_id=1&click_id=22&art_id=vn20050129114540161C803463|url-status=live}} He clarified the issue and said "We never intended them to be gay. I consider them to be almost [[Asexuality|asexual]]. We're just trying to be funny and this has got nothing to do with the show."{{cite news | url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/2313221.stm | title=Camp cartoon star 'is not gay' | date=October 9, 2002 | access-date=June 11, 2007 | author=BBC Staff | publisher=[[BBC News]] | archive-date=November 7, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151107044940/http://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/entertainment/tv_and_radio/2313221.stm | url-status=live }}{{cite web | url=http://www.people.com/people/article/0,,1021976,00.html | title=SpongeBob Asexual, Not Gay: Creator | date=January 28, 2005 | access-date=August 26, 2009 | first=Stephen M. | last=Silverman | work=[[People (magazine)|People]] | archive-date=March 20, 2008 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080320034827/http://www.people.com/people/article/0,,1021976,00.html }} Tom Kenny and other production members were shocked and surprised that such an issue had arisen.{{cite video|people=Farhat, Basima (Interviewer) |date=December 5, 2006 |title=Tom Kenny: Voice of SpongeBob SquarePants – Interview |url=http://www.thepeoplespeakradio.net/archives/mp3/tps-2006-12-05-kenny.mp3 |format=mp3 |medium=Radio production |publisher=The People Speak Radio |access-date=November 8, 2008 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724101824/http://www.thepeoplespeakradio.net/archives/mp3/tps-2006-12-05-kenny.mp3 |archive-date=July 24, 2011 }} [[Derek Drymon]], the show's [[creative director]] until 2004, said, "If SpongeBob holds hands with Patrick it's because he's his best friend and he loves him. I think the whole thing is a part of a larger agenda to stigmatize gay people." Focus on the Family founder [[James Dobson]] later stated that his comments were taken out of context and that his original complaints were not with SpongeBob or any of the characters in the video but with the organization that sponsored the video, the [[We Are Family Foundation]]. Dobson noted that the foundation had posted pro-homosexual material on its website, but later removed it.{{cite web |url=https://www.christianpost.com/news/dobson-clarifies-pro-gay-spongebob-video-controversy-20875/ |title=Dobson clarifies Pro-Gay SpongeBob Video Controversy |last=Chang |first=Pauline J. |date=January 28, 2005 |newspaper=The Christian Post |access-date=May 18, 2018 |archive-date=July 21, 2012 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120721232727/http://www.christianpost.com/article/20050128/20875.htm |url-status=live }} [[Queer theory|Queer theorist]] Jeffrey P. Dennis, author of the journal article "The Same Thing We Do Every Night: Signifying Same-Sex Desire in Television Cartoons", argued that SpongeBob and [[Sandy Cheeks|Sandy]] are not romantically in love, while adding that he believed that SpongeBob and Patrick "are paired with arguably erotic intensity". Dennis noted the two are "not consistently coded as romantic partners", since they live in separate residences, and have distinct groups of friends, but claimed that in the series, "the possibility of same-sex desire is never excluded."Dennis, Jeffrey P. "[http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01956050309603674 The Same Thing We Do Every Night: Signifying Same-Sex Desire in Television Cartoons] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190124041715/https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/01956050309603674 |date=January 24, 2019 }}." ''[[Journal of Popular Film & Television]]''. Fall 2003. Volume 31, Issue 3. 132–140. 9p, 3bw.
